papers_seen.author: Duran
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and model compression have emerged as fundamental techniques for transferring knowledge from large, computationally expensive neural networks (teacher models) to smaller, more efficient student models. These methods address critical practical deployment constraints including inference latency, memory consumption, computational efficiency, and device heterogeneity while maintaining competitive performance. Knowledge distillation mechanisms span multiple approaches—from output-level soft-target matching to intermediate feature and layer-level alignment—and can be combined with complementary compression techniques such as pruning, quantization, and architecture search. The field encompasses diverse applications across computer vision, natural language processing, speech recognition, and other domains, serving as a central, versatile toolkit for enabling efficient model deployment in resource-constrained environments.

papers_seen.author: Hicks
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful technique for model compression and knowledge transfer in deep learning and NLP applications. By enabling the transfer of knowledge from large teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models, knowledge distillation addresses critical challenges of inference speed, memory consumption, and computational resource requirements. This approach has been successfully applied across diverse domains including NLP tasks, computer vision, federated learning, and various specialized applications, offering practical solutions for deploying complex models in resource-constrained environments.

papers_seen.author: Wilson
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Techniques for Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and allied model-compression techniques transform large, high-capacity models into smaller, faster, or more specialized models while retaining much of the original performance. The approaches span matching teacher soft outputs, imitating intermediate representations, many-to-many layer mapping, data augmentation during transfer, data-free distillation, and architecture-aware compression. Practical systems combine distillation with neural architecture search, federated or privacy-preserving protocols, and multimodal adaptation to meet deployment constraints such as latency, memory, heterogeneity of devices, and absence of original training data. This synthesis summarizes key methods, empirical insights, and deployment-oriented strategies developed to date.

papers_seen.author: Stewart
papers_seen.title: The Case for Knowledge Distillation as a Core Tool for Model Compression Across Modalities
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured into a flexible, domain-agnostic strategy that enables deployment of high-performing deep models in resource-constrained settings. By transferring predictive behavior, intermediate representations, or distilled data between teacher and student, KD supports compression of generators, discriminative models, and multimodal systems, while enabling privacy-preserving and data-free workflows. When combined with careful pre-training, many-to-many layer alignment, or generative replay, KD allows compact architectures to approach the performance of large teachers and, in some cases, inherit desirable properties such as robustness or interpretability. This paper argues that KD should be treated as a foundational method in model compression toolkits and proposes practical emphases for future work: preserving internal representations, supporting data-free distillation, leveraging pre-training for small models, and distilling robustness.

papers_seen.author: Alvarez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Contextual Strategy for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and flexible approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students while preserving much of teacher performance. KD is not a single algorithm but a toolkit of mechanisms (soft targets, intermediate-representation matching, attention and relational objectives, multi-teacher curricula, and data-aware variants) that, when combined with complementary compression methods and careful design, enables efficient deployment across vision and language tasks. Effective use of KD requires attention to teacher–student capacity alignment, data availability and privacy, robustness under distribution shift, and integration with quantization, pruning, or architecture transformations. I argue KD should be treated as a central, composable component of compression pipelines and applied with task-aware practices rather than as an off-the-shelf panacea.

papers_seen.author: Parsons
papers_seen.title: Curriculum Learning for Dense Retrieval Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Recent work has shown that more effective dense retrieval models can be obtained by distilling ranking knowledge from an existing base re-ranking model. In this paper, we propose a generic curriculum learning based optimization framework called CL-DRD that controls the difficulty level of training data produced by the re-ranking (teacher) model. CL-DRD iteratively optimizes the dense retrieval (student) model by increasing the difficulty of the knowledge distillation data made available to it. In more detail, we initially provide the student model coarse-grained preference pairs between documents in the teacher's ranking and progressively move towards finer-grained pairwise document ordering requirements. In our experiments, we apply a simple implementation of the CL-DRD framework to enhance two state-of-the-art dense retrieval models. Experiments on three public passage retrieval datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of our proposed framework.

papers_seen.author: Wyatt
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Context-Aware Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and versatile approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. When treated as a core, composable component of compression pipelines and combined with task-aware design, KD yields strong efficiency–accuracy tradeoffs across vision, language, speech, and recommendation systems. However, KD is not a plug-and-play cure: its success depends on what signals are transferred, teacher–student alignment, data availability and privacy constraints, and attention to robustness and rare-case behaviors. Practical deployment therefore requires multi-signal distillation, student-aware teacher design, and integration with complementary compression techniques.

papers_seen.author: Powers
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central strategy for compressing large, high-performing neural networks into smaller, more efficient models by transferring knowledge from a teacher to a student. Research over the past decade has produced a diverse set of distillation objectives (soft-target/logit matching, feature- and attention-level imitation, contrastive and adversarial formulations), integration with complementary compression techniques (pruning, layer skipping, architecture search, quantization), and methods for operating under deployment constraints (domain adaptation, data-free distillation, ensemble teachers). Empirical studies across vision, language, multimodal, and industrial prediction tasks demonstrate that carefully chosen distillation formulations and teacher-student pairings yield substantial gains in efficiency with limited accuracy loss, while ongoing challenges remain in handling domain shift, teacher errors, and task-specific desiderata.

papers_seen.author: Murillo
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Essential Techniques for Practical Deep Learning Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression have become fundamental techniques for deploying large, high-performing deep learning models in resource-constrained environments. By transferring knowledge from larger teacher models to smaller student models, these methods enable substantial reductions in parameter count, memory consumption, and inference latency while maintaining competitive accuracy. These approaches have been successfully adapted across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, speech recognition, and graph neural networks, with emerging variants addressing specific challenges such as fairness, privacy preservation, and task-adaptive compression.

papers_seen.author: Schwartz
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Applications, and Practical Considerations
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a fundamental and versatile technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient student models while preserving competitive performance. By transferring knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to resource-constrained students, KD enables practical deployment across vision, language, and specialized domains. This synthesis examines the core mechanisms of knowledge distillation, its diverse applications, and critical design considerations for achieving effective compression in real-world settings.

papers_seen.author: Camacho
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: Essential, Composable, and Context-Sensitive for Practical Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations. KD supports multiple transfer signals (soft targets, intermediate features, relational structure) and protocols (offline, online, multi-teacher, data-free) and is most effective when integrated with complementary compression methods and matched to deployment constraints. While KD routinely offers strong size–performance trade-offs, realizing those gains in practice requires task- and data-aware design, careful teacher–student alignment, and evaluation for robustness and undesirable behavior.

papers_seen.author: Cox
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Default for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, engineering-oriented approach to compressing large models into deployable students. By transferring predictive behavior and internal representations through configurable signals, and by composing naturally with pruning, quantization, architecture adaptation, and data-aware strategies, KD routinely produces favorable efficiency–accuracy tradeoffs in language and vision systems. Realizing these gains in production demands task-aware design: choosing appropriate distillation signals, aligning teacher and student capacity, handling limited or private data, and diagnosing robustness, fairness, and distribution-shift risks. When applied as a composable toolkit with explicit monitoring and complementary compression methods, KD provides a practical route to efficient, high-performance models for real-world deployment.

papers_seen.author: Campbell
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Comprehensive Overview
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a fundamental technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, deployable models while maintaining competitive performance. By transferring knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to resource-constrained student networks, KD enables practical deployment of state-of-the-art deep learning and NLP systems under stringent latency, memory, and privacy constraints. The approach encompasses diverse mechanisms ranging from soft-target matching to feature-level and attention-based transfers, and can be strategically combined with complementary compression techniques. However, successful implementation requires careful, task-aware design choices that account for teacher-student capacity alignment, data availability, and domain-specific considerations.

papers_seen.author: Walker
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Fundamental Approach to Deep Learning Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a transformative technique for compressing neural networks while maintaining predictive performance. By enabling knowledge transfer from large teacher models to compact student networks, distillation addresses the critical challenge of deploying sophisticated deep learning systems on resource-constrained devices. This paper argues that knowledge distillation represents an essential methodology for practical machine learning deployment, offering significant advantages in model size reduction, computational efficiency, and accessibility across diverse application domains from natural language processing to computer vision.

papers_seen.author: Payne
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as an Essential Framework for Practical Deep Learning Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and versatile technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, efficient student models while maintaining competitive performance. By transferring knowledge from high-capacity teacher models through diverse mechanisms such as soft-target matching, intermediate representation alignment, and attention-based transfers, knowledge distillation enables significant reductions in model size, computational cost, and inference latency. When integrated as a composable core component of broader compression pipelines and adapted to task-specific constraints, knowledge distillation represents an essential engineering paradigm for bringing state-of-the-art deep learning models into practical deployment across vision, language, and specialized domains.

papers_seen.author: Higgins
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile practical strategy for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students that retain much of teacher capability. KD succeeds across modalities by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations and is most effective when combined with complementary compression techniques and careful teacher–student design. However, its success is context-sensitive: choices about what form of knowledge to transfer, how to align architectures, how to handle limited or private data, and how to adapt to distribution shift determine whether a distilled student meets deployment requirements. This paper argues that KD should be treated as a default, composable toolkit for model compression in deep learning and NLP, applied with task-aware engineering and attention to its known limits.

papers_seen.author: Francis
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Essential Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and versatile technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. By transferring knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to resource-constrained student models, knowledge distillation addresses critical deployment challenges including reduced latency, memory footprint, and computational cost across diverse domains such as computer vision, natural language processing, machine translation, and speech recognition. However, effective distillation requires careful orchestration of multiple design choices, including the selection of distillation targets, teacher-student capacity alignment, data strategies, and integration with complementary compression techniques to achieve reliable results.

papers_seen.author: Williams
papers_seen.title: Linkless Link Prediction via Relational Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) have shown exceptional performance in the task of link prediction. Despite their effectiveness, the high latency brought by non-trivial neighborhood data dependency limits GNNs in practical deployments. Conversely, the known efficient MLPs are much less effective than GNNs due to the lack of relational knowledge. In this work, to combine the advantages of GNNs and MLPs, we start with exploring direct knowledge distillation (KD) methods for link prediction, i.e., predicted logit-based matching and node representation-based matching. Upon observing direct KD analogs do not perform well for link prediction, we propose a relational KD framework, Linkless Link Prediction (LLP), to distill knowledge for link prediction with MLPs. Unlike simple KD methods that match independent link logits or node representations, LLP distills relational knowledge that is centered around each (anchor) node to the student MLP. Specifically, we propose rank-based matching and distribution-based matching strategies that complement each other. Extensive experiments demonstrate that LLP boosts the link prediction performance of MLPs with significant margins, and even outperforms the teacher GNNs on 7 out of 8 benchmarks. LLP also achieves a 70.68x speedup in link prediction inference compared to GNNs on the large-scale OGB dataset.

papers_seen.author: Cowan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as an Essential Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and versatile approach to compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students while retaining much of their performance. KD techniques range from classic soft-logit matching to feature- and layer-wise transfer, and they enable deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. However, realizing KD's benefits requires task- and architecture-aware choices: what to distill (logits, features, internal layers), how to handle limited or private data, and how to align teacher-student capacities. When combined with principled practices, KD is indispensable for translating research-scale models into robust, efficient production systems.

papers_seen.author: Webster
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and versatile technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. By transferring knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to resource-constrained student networks, knowledge distillation enables practical deployment of state-of-the-art deep learning and natural language processing systems in resource-limited environments. The approach encompasses diverse strategies ranging from soft-target matching and intermediate feature alignment to multi-teacher approaches and data-free variants, addressing critical real-world challenges including computational efficiency, inference latency, memory constraints, and privacy preservation across multiple domains.

papers_seen.author: Williams
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Comprehensive Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and versatile technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, deployable models suitable for resource-constrained environments. This synthesis examines the mechanisms, methodologies, practical applications, and remaining challenges in knowledge distillation across deep learning and natural language processing. Knowledge distillation enables practitioners to transfer knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to efficient student models while maintaining competitive performance, addressing critical deployment constraints including computational cost, memory consumption, inference latency, and energy efficiency. The field has evolved from simple soft-target matching to a comprehensive toolkit encompassing multiple transfer mechanisms, complementary compression strategies, and task-aware design principles.

papers_seen.author: Moon
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Context-Aware Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and versatile method for producing compact models by transferring information from large teacher models to smaller students. When used as part of a broader compression pipeline—together with pruning, quantization, architecture-aware design, and data-aware strategies—KD enables deployment of high-performing models under latency, memory, and device constraints. However, distillation is not a universal cure: its effectiveness depends on choices about what to transfer, how to prepare or synthesize distillation data, teacher–student capacity alignment, and explicit handling of robustness, fairness, and domain shift. A principled, task-aware KD strategy that integrates complementary techniques and monitoring yields the most reliable path to deployable, efficient models in both deep learning and NLP.

papers_seen.author: Murphy
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation in Deep Learning and NLP: Powerful, Context-Dependent, and Best Deployed as an Integrated Strategy
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and practically essential approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students while preserving much of teacher performance. KD methods range from soft-target matching to representation alignment and staged or multi-teacher procedures. Their empirical success across vision and language tasks makes KD a central tool for production deployment on resource-constrained hardware, but its effectiveness depends on careful matching of objectives, data, and student capacity. I argue that KD should be treated as a toolkit to be combined with privacy, robustness, and fairness-aware practices rather than a one-size-fits-all solution.

papers_seen.author: Brown
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Comprehensive Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and versatile technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, deployable student models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach transfers knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to resource-constrained students, enabling efficient deployment across diverse domains. Knowledge distillation encompasses multiple mechanisms and methodologies, including soft-target matching, intermediate representation alignment, and data-aware strategies. When treated as a composable framework combined with complementary compression techniques, knowledge distillation addresses critical practical challenges including computational efficiency, memory constraints, inference latency, and privacy preservation in both deep learning and natural language processing applications.

papers_seen.author: Harmon
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Composable Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile family of techniques that enables high-performing models to be deployed under resource constraints by transferring behavior, representations, or synthesized signals from larger teachers to smaller students. When treated as a composable, task-aware component of compression toolkits—combined with pruning, quantization, architecture search, or data synthesis—KD routinely yields practical size–performance tradeoffs. However, realizing reliable outcomes requires careful teacher selection, objective design, curriculum and data strategies, and explicit attention to failure modes such as optimization gaps, capacity mismatch, and the transfer of undesirable behaviors.

papers_seen.author: Cox
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central Strategy for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and versatile technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, deployable models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach transfers knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to resource-constrained student networks, enabling practical deployment across diverse domains. The technique encompasses multiple complementary methodologies including soft-target matching, intermediate feature alignment, multi-teacher schemes, and data-aware variants. When thoughtfully applied as an integrated toolkit combined with complementary compression techniques, knowledge distillation represents the most practical and broadly applicable approach to achieving efficient neural networks suitable for real-world deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints.

papers_seen.author: Richards
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Essential Techniques for Practical Deep Learning Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression have emerged as critical techniques for enabling the deployment of large, powerful neural networks in resource-constrained environments. These methods transfer knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to smaller student models, achieving substantial reductions in model size, computational cost, and inference latency while maintaining competitive predictive performance. Applications span diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, machine translation, and specialized tasks. Knowledge distillation should be understood as a flexible, composable toolkit rather than a one-size-fits-all solution, requiring careful consideration of what knowledge to transfer, student capacity, data availability, and integration with complementary compression strategies.

papers_seen.author: Barnes
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Composable Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile model-compression family that transfers information from large teacher models to smaller students to enable deployment under strict latency, memory, and privacy constraints. When treated as a core, composable operation—combined with pruning, quantization, architecture design, and task-aware training—KD consistently yields compact models that retain a large portion of teacher performance. However, realizing reliable, production-grade distillation requires multi-objective design (what to transfer, how to weight signals, and how to handle data constraints), careful attention to teacher–student capacity alignment, and explicit evaluation of robustness, fairness, and failure modes. Practically, KD should be adopted as a central element of compression toolkits while being used with explicit safeguards and complementary methods to address its empirical and theoretical limits.

papers_seen.author: Gonzalez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Applications, and Open Challenges
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses high-capacity models into smaller ones by transferring predictive behavior or internal structure from a teacher to a student. Recent work has expanded KD beyond matching output probabilities to include internal representation matching, flexible layer alignment, multi-teacher training, data-free approaches, and privacy-aware compression. These advances have been applied to NLP (notably BERT compression), vision, graphs, and other domains, while open challenges remain around data heterogeneity, layer alignment, and robust data-free training.

papers_seen.author: Brennan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Applications, and Practical Challenges
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a fundamental and versatile technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. Rather than a single algorithmic recipe, KD represents a flexible framework that encompasses multiple mechanisms for transferring knowledge from teacher to student models, ranging from soft output distributions to intermediate representations and feature-level imitation. The approach enables significant reductions in model size, memory requirements, and inference latency across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, and specialized applications. While KD provides substantial practical benefits for real-world deployment under resource constraints, its effectiveness depends critically on careful design choices about teacher-student alignment, data availability, what forms of knowledge to transfer, and integration with complementary compression strategies. Practical success also requires attention to handling optimization barriers, bias transfer, and distributional robustness concerns.

papers_seen.author: Bowen
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large, high-capacity models into smaller, deployable students by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations through a range of mechanisms. The approach has evolved from matching softened output logits to a broader toolkit that includes intermediate-feature mimicry, attention and relational transfer, data-augmentation and data-free strategies, and combinations with pruning, quantization, and architecture adaptation. While distillation routinely yields substantial efficiency gains with modest performance loss, its success depends on student capacity, teacher quality, data availability, and careful choice of what and how to transfer; attention to optimization dynamics, robustness, and bias transfer is necessary for reliable deployment.

papers_seen.author: Nguyen
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large neural models into smaller, deployable students by transferring predictive behavior, softened outputs, intermediate representations, or structural behaviors. KD is a flexible, composable component of modern compression pipelines: it can be combined with pruning, quantization, architecture search, and data synthesis to meet latency, memory, and hardware constraints while often preserving most of the teacher’s performance. Practical success depends on careful choices about what to transfer, teacher–student alignment, data availability, optimization dynamics, and task-aware design; open challenges include robust data-free distillation, bias and robustness transfer, and principled teacher selection.

papers_seen.author: Henderson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Applications, and Practical Considerations
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression have emerged as essential techniques for deploying large deep neural networks in resource-constrained environments. These methods enable the transfer of knowledge from large, complex teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models while preserving predictive performance. Applications span computer vision, natural language processing, speech recognition, and other domains, with diverse approaches adapted to specific task requirements and deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Osborne
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a widely-adopted technique for training compact and efficient models by transferring knowledge from large teacher models to smaller student models. This approach has become instrumental across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, and specialized applications like graph neural networks and recommender systems. The technique addresses the fundamental challenge of deploying sophisticated deep learning models in resource-constrained environments while maintaining competitive performance levels. Recent advances have expanded the methodology beyond simple output probability matching to include intermediate representations, multi-teacher frameworks, and integration with complementary compression techniques.

papers_seen.author: Hill
papers_seen.title: A Deep Hierarchical Approach to Lifelong Learning in Minecraft
papers_seen.abstract: We propose a lifelong learning system that has the ability to reuse and transfer knowledge from one task to another while efficiently retaining the previously learned knowledge-base. Knowledge is transferred by learning reusable skills to solve tasks in Minecraft, a popular video game which is an unsolved and high-dimensional lifelong learning problem. These reusable skills, which we refer to as Deep Skill Networks, are then incorporated into our novel Hierarchical Deep Reinforcement Learning Network (H-DRLN) architecture using two techniques: (1) a deep skill array and (2) skill distillation, our novel variation of policy distillation (Rusu et. al. 2015) for learning skills. Skill distillation enables the HDRLN to efficiently retain knowledge and therefore scale in lifelong learning, by accumulating knowledge and encapsulating multiple reusable skills into a single distilled network. The H-DRLN exhibits superior performance and lower learning sample complexity compared to the regular Deep Q Network (Mnih et. al. 2015) in sub-domains of Minecraft.

papers_seen.author: Roman
papers_seen.title: Fair Feature Distillation for Visual Recognition
papers_seen.abstract: Fairness is becoming an increasingly crucial issue for computer vision, especially in the human-related decision systems. However, achieving algorithmic fairness, which makes a model produce indiscriminative outcomes against protected groups, is still an unresolved problem. In this paper, we devise a systematic approach which reduces algorithmic biases via feature distillation for visual recognition tasks, dubbed as MMD-based Fair Distillation (MFD). While the distillation technique has been widely used in general to improve the prediction accuracy, to the best of our knowledge, there has been no explicit work that also tries to improve fairness via distillation. Furthermore, We give a theoretical justification of our MFD on the effect of knowledge distillation and fairness. Throughout the extensive experiments, we show our MFD significantly mitigates the bias against specific minorities without any loss of the accuracy on both synthetic and real-world face datasets.

papers_seen.author: Nolan
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, empirically effective framework for compressing large teacher models into smaller student models suitable for deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. KD encompasses a range of objectives and design choices—matching soft outputs, aligning intermediate representations, using ensembles or multi-teacher schedules, and combining with architecture search, pruning, or quantization—to balance efficiency and task performance. Practical success depends on matching teacher-student capacity, selecting what to transfer, handling data availability (including data-free or synthesized data), and adapting distillation strategies to task-specific constraints. KD has been adapted across vision and language tasks and continues to evolve via techniques that improve transferability, training efficiency, fairness, and robustness.

papers_seen.author: Hernandez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Comprehensive Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and versatile technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, deployable student models while maintaining competitive performance. The approach transfers knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to resource-constrained students through a diverse family of mechanisms, enabling practical deployment across computer vision, natural language processing, speech processing, and specialized domains. This synthesis examines the core mechanisms of knowledge distillation, its complementary compression strategies, practical applications, and remaining challenges in achieving efficient deep learning deployment.

papers_seen.author: Shaffer
papers_seen.title: Selective Knowledge Distillation for Neural Machine Translation
papers_seen.abstract: Neural Machine Translation (NMT) models achieve state-of-the-art performance on many translation benchmarks. As an active research field in NMT, knowledge distillation is widely applied to enhance the model's performance by transferring teacher model's knowledge on each training sample. However, previous work rarely discusses the different impacts and connections among these samples, which serve as the medium for transferring teacher knowledge. In this paper, we design a novel protocol that can effectively analyze the different impacts of samples by comparing various samples' partitions. Based on above protocol, we conduct extensive experiments and find that the teacher's knowledge is not the more, the better. Knowledge over specific samples may even hurt the whole performance of knowledge distillation. Finally, to address these issues, we propose two simple yet effective strategies, i.e., batch-level and global-level selections, to pick suitable samples for distillation. We evaluate our approaches on two large-scale machine translation tasks, WMT'14 English->German and WMT'19 Chinese->English. Experimental results show that our approaches yield up to +1.28 and +0.89 BLEU points improvements over the Transformer baseline, respectively.

papers_seen.author: Walker
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Default Strategy for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a fundamental and versatile technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models suitable for deployment in resource-constrained environments. This paper argues that KD should serve as the default starting point for model compression across deep learning and NLP applications, as it consistently delivers substantial reductions in model size and inference latency while preserving much of the teacher's performance. However, successful implementation requires careful attention to design choices, complementary compression techniques, and task-specific constraints rather than treating KD as a universal one-size-fits-all solution.

papers_seen.author: Hall
papers_seen.title: FedZKT: Zero-Shot Knowledge Transfer towards Resource-Constrained Federated Learning with Heterogeneous On-Device Models
papers_seen.abstract: Federated learning enables multiple distributed devices to collaboratively learn a shared prediction model without centralizing their on-device data. Most of the current algorithms require comparable individual efforts for local training with the same structure and size of on-device models, which, however, impedes participation from resource-constrained devices. Given the widespread yet heterogeneous devices nowadays, in this paper, we propose an innovative federated learning framework with heterogeneous on-device models through Zero-shot Knowledge Transfer, named by FedZKT. Specifically, FedZKT allows devices to independently determine the on-device models upon their local resources. To achieve knowledge transfer across these heterogeneous on-device models, a zero-shot distillation approach is designed without any prerequisites for private on-device data, which is contrary to certain prior research based on a public dataset or a pre-trained data generator. Moreover, this compute-intensive distillation task is assigned to the server to allow the participation of resource-constrained devices, where a generator is adversarially learned with the ensemble of collected on-device models. The distilled central knowledge is then sent back in the form of the corresponding on-device model parameters, which can be easily absorbed on the device side. Extensive experimental studies demonstrate the effectiveness and robustness of FedZKT towards on-device knowledge agnostic, on-device model heterogeneity, and other challenging federated learning scenarios, such as heterogeneous on-device data and straggler effects.

papers_seen.author: Levy
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Default for Model Compression: Strengths, Limits, and Deployment Guidelines
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, empirically validated framework for compressing large teacher models into smaller student models that meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints while preserving much of task performance. KD spans output-level supervision, internal-representation matching, ensemble and online schemes, and data-free or federated protocols. Its reliability in production depends on matching distillation signals to student capacity, addressing data constraints (including synthesized or private data), and combining KD with complementary compression methods and diagnostics to handle distribution shift, rare-token behavior, and device heterogeneity. When applied as a composable element of a broader compression pipeline and tuned for deployment constraints, KD routinely yields efficient models suitable for real-world NLP and deep-learning systems.

papers_seen.author: Valencia
papers_seen.title: Compression of Deep Learning Models for Text: A Survey
papers_seen.abstract: In recent years, the fields of natural language processing (NLP) and information retrieval (IR) have made tremendous progress thanksto deep learning models like Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs), Gated Recurrent Units (GRUs) and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTMs)networks, and Transformer [120] based models like Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers (BERT) [24], GenerativePre-training Transformer (GPT-2) [94], Multi-task Deep Neural Network (MT-DNN) [73], Extra-Long Network (XLNet) [134], Text-to-text transfer transformer (T5) [95], T-NLG [98] and GShard [63]. But these models are humongous in size. On the other hand,real world applications demand small model size, low response times and low computational power wattage. In this survey, wediscuss six different types of methods (Pruning, Quantization, Knowledge Distillation, Parameter Sharing, Tensor Decomposition, andSub-quadratic Transformer based methods) for compression of such models to enable their deployment in real industry NLP projects.Given the critical need of building applications with efficient and small models, and the large amount of recently published work inthis area, we believe that this survey organizes the plethora of work done by the 'deep learning for NLP' community in the past fewyears and presents it as a coherent story.

papers_seen.author: Dodson
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) reduces model size and inference cost by transferring information from a high-capacity teacher to a compact student. A broad family of KD methods has been developed, ranging from matching teacher output distributions to aligning intermediate representations and designing layer-wise or relational objectives. Practitioners combine KD with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and data-centric strategies (augmentation, synthetic or unlabeled data) to produce deployable models that retain much of the teacher’s performance. Empirical work shows KD improves generalization under limited-data regimes, recovers accuracy for low-precision networks, and can be adapted to heterogeneous or structured tasks such as graph link prediction. Key challenges include teacher–student capacity mismatch, dependence on data availability or privacy, and preserving rare or domain-specific behaviors; current directions emphasize student-aware teacher design, feature-level transfer, data augmentation, and task-aware objectives to mitigate these issues.

papers_seen.author: Nguyen
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: A Context-Sensitive Toolbox for Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a pragmatic and widely applicable strategy for compressing large deep learning models into smaller, deployable students. KD routinely yields strong size–performance trade-offs when applied with attention to teacher–student capacity alignment, choice of distillation targets, and data or task constraints. However, KD is not a universal solution: its reliability in production depends on diagnosing transfer failures (robustness, rare events, and bias), combining KD with complementary compression techniques, and adopting task- or deployment-aware design choices. This paper argues that KD should be treated as the default starting point for compression pipelines, applied as a flexible, composed toolkit and augmented where diagnostics indicate limits.

papers_seen.author: Tucker
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Essential Framework for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP

By transferring knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to resource-constrained student networks, knowledge distillation enables efficient deployment across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, and specialized applications. This paper argues that knowledge distillation should serve as the central framework for model compression, particularly when carefully combined with complementary techniques and adapted to specific task, data, and hardware constraints.

Through teacher-student learning frameworks, knowledge distillation transfers learned representations from complex models to compact ones, addressing the critical challenge of balancing model capacity with computational efficiency across vision and language tasks.

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a versatile and empirically effective approach for compressing large neural networks into smaller, deployable student models while preserving competitive performance. Rather than a single technique, knowledge distillation represents a flexible, composable framework that transfers knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to resource-constrained students through multiple complementary mechanisms. When thoughtfully combined with additional compression strategies and adapted to specific task and deployment constraints, knowledge distillation enables practical deployment of state-of-the-art deep learning and NLP systems across diverse domains while addressing critical challenges in computational efficiency, inference latency, memory consumption, and privacy.

papers_seen.author: Norris
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Foundational Strategy for Practical Neural Network Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation represents a versatile and essential approach for compressing large neural networks into smaller, deployable models suitable for resource-constrained environments. By systematically transferring knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to compact student networks, knowledge distillation addresses critical real-world deployment constraints including computational efficiency, memory limitations, inference latency, and privacy concerns. This technique has evolved from simple output-level matching to a comprehensive toolkit encompassing multiple transfer mechanisms and complementary strategies, enabling practical deployment of state-of-the-art deep learning systems across diverse domains with maintained competitive performance.

papers_seen.author: Schultz
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has become a core practical tool for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students in deep learning and NLP. The technique has expanded from simple softened-logit matching to a rich toolkit that includes intermediate-feature and layer-wise transfer, attention and relational objectives, multi-teacher and online schemes, and data-aware variants (including data-free and privacy-preserving workflows). When combined with complementary techniques such as pruning, quantization, and architecture search, KD enables large reductions in model size and inference cost with modest performance loss. However, its success depends on careful teacher–student alignment, appropriate distillation targets, data strategies, and evaluation focused on robustness and task-specific phenomena; theoretical and practical limits remain in settings with mismatched capacities, limited or private data, and distribution shift.

papers_seen.author: Knight
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Current Understanding and Practical Applications
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a foundational and practical technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient student models while maintaining competitive performance across deep learning and natural language processing tasks. By transferring knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to resource-constrained students, KD enables deployment of state-of-the-art systems with reduced inference latency, memory footprint, and computational cost. The field has evolved from simple logit matching to sophisticated multi-faceted approaches incorporating intermediate representation alignment, multi-teacher schemes, and data-aware strategies. However, KD's effectiveness is not universal and depends critically on careful design choices regarding what knowledge to transfer, teacher-student alignment, data availability, and task-specific considerations.

papers_seen.author: Byrd
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Default for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Strengths, Limits, and Design Guidelines
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured into a versatile, empirically effective approach for turning large teacher models into smaller, deployable students. As a composable toolkit that includes soft-target matching, intermediate-feature alignment, ensemble-to-single-model transfer, and data-centric distillation strategies, KD can deliver substantial reductions in inference cost while preserving much of teacher performance. However, its success depends on careful, task-aware choices about what signals to transfer, how to align student capacity with teacher signals, and how to combine distillation with complementary compression methods. Treating KD as the default compression backbone—applied with explicit design rules, data strategies, and hybrid compression—enables practical, efficient deployment of modern deep learning and NLP systems.

papers_seen.author: Rhodes
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, widely adopted framework for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students by transferring information beyond hard labels. Across vision, language, multimodal, and specialized domains, KD methods operate at multiple levels of abstraction (output logits, intermediate representations, attention maps, relational objectives) and are frequently combined with complementary compression strategies (pruning, quantization, and architecture search). Practical success depends on principled teacher–student alignment, data strategies (pretraining, augmentation, synthetic or data‑free approaches), and task‑aware adaptations. Open problems include principled student architecture selection, preserving robustness and fairness under compression, handling limited or private data, mitigating transfer of undesirable teacher behaviors, and better theoretical understanding of when distillation aids generalization.

papers_seen.author: Mitchell
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Theory, Applications, and Limits
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large or ensemble teacher models into smaller student models by transferring information beyond hard labels. A mature toolkit now includes soft-target (logit) matching, intermediate-feature and attention imitation, multi-stage and multi-teacher pipelines, data-free or synthesized-data strategies, and privacy-aware variants. Distillation has been applied to vision, language, graphs, generative models, and healthcare, producing substantial inference and deployment gains while exposing limits arising from optimization, teacher–student mismatch, and data constraints. Progress requires carefully matching the distilled signals to student capacity, combining distillation with complementary compression methods, and addressing theoretical and practical failure modes to ensure robustness, fairness, and privacy.

papers_seen.author: Stewart
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as an Essential, Practically Flexible Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central, practical strategy for compressing large neural models into deployable students while preserving much of the teacher’s capabilities. KD techniques span matching teacher logits, aligning internal features, and using multi-teacher or teacher-free schedules; they enable large speedups and memory reductions, adapt to privacy- and data-limited settings, and have been successfully applied across retrieval, graph learning, generative models, and pretrained NLP transformers. The choice of what to transfer (outputs vs. intermediate representations), how to weight multiple sources, and whether to rely on original data fundamentally shapes outcomes. I argue that KD is indispensable for real-world deep learning deployment, but progress will require tighter practices for representation alignment, student-friendly teacher design, and handling heterogeneous or private data.

papers_seen.author: Ellis
papers_seen.title: On Representation Knowledge Distillation for Graph Neural Networks
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a learning paradigm for boosting resource-efficient graph neural networks (GNNs) using more expressive yet cumbersome teacher models. Past work on distillation for GNNs proposed the Local Structure Preserving loss (LSP), which matches local structural relationships defined over edges across the student and teacher's node embeddings. This paper studies whether preserving the global topology of how the teacher embeds graph data can be a more effective distillation objective for GNNs, as real-world graphs often contain latent interactions and noisy edges. We propose Graph Contrastive Representation Distillation (G-CRD), which uses contrastive learning to implicitly preserve global topology by aligning the student node embeddings to those of the teacher in a shared representation space. Additionally, we introduce an expanded set of benchmarks on large-scale real-world datasets where the performance gap between teacher and student GNNs is non-negligible. Experiments across 4 datasets and 14 heterogeneous GNN architectures show that G-CRD consistently boosts the performance and robustness of lightweight GNNs, outperforming LSP (and a global structure preserving variant of LSP) as well as baselines from 2D computer vision. An analysis of the representational similarity among teacher and student embedding spaces reveals that G-CRD balances preserving local and global relationships, while structure preserving approaches are best at preserving one or the other. Our code is available at https://github.com/chaitjo/efficient-gnns

papers_seen.author: Gomez
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large neural networks into smaller, deployable models by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from teacher to student. Over the past decade KD has broadened from soft-target (logit) matching to a toolbox that includes intermediate-feature and attention transfer, multi- and self-distillation, data- and privacy-aware variants, and integration with complementary compression methods (e.g., pruning, quantization, architecture search). Empirical evidence shows KD can preserve much of teacher performance while reducing inference cost, but success depends on careful choices about what signals to transfer, teacher–student alignment, data strategies, and evaluation under distribution shift. This synthesis summarizes mechanisms, empirical patterns, practical guidelines, and common limitations reported across recent literature.

papers_seen.author: Rios
papers_seen.title: Improving Neural Topic Models using Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Topic models are often used to identify human-interpretable topics to help make sense of large document collections. We use knowledge distillation to combine the best attributes of probabilistic topic models and pretrained transformers. Our modular method can be straightforwardly applied with any neural topic model to improve topic quality, which we demonstrate using two models having disparate architectures, obtaining state-of-the-art topic coherence. We show that our adaptable framework not only improves performance in the aggregate over all estimated topics, as is commonly reported, but also in head-to-head comparisons of aligned topics.

papers_seen.author: Lucas
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile family of methods for transferring behavior from large teacher models to smaller student models to reduce storage, latency, and compute while retaining much of the teacher’s performance. KD encompasses output-level supervision, intermediate-representation matching, multi-teacher and data-free variants, and online or adversarial feature-level transfers. In practice KD is most effective when treated as a component of a larger compression pipeline (pruning, quantization, architecture design) and when practitioners attend to teacher–student alignment, data availability, and risks such as robustness and bias transfer.

papers_seen.author: Williams
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Composable, Task-Aware Core for Practical Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, versatile technique for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. When treated as a composable component within broader compression pipelines—together with pruning, quantization, and architecture search—and adapted to task constraints and data regimes, KD yields strong efficiency–accuracy trade-offs. However, reliable deployment requires explicit attention to teacher–student capacity alignment, optimization dynamics, data availability and distribution shift, and targeted evaluation of robustness and low-frequency behaviors.
