papers_seen.author: Thomas
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, empirically effective approach for compressing large teacher models into smaller, deployable student models in deep learning and NLP. By transferring richer supervision than hard labels—via softened outputs, layer-wise feature targets, attention maps, or ensembles—KD enables strong size/performance trade-offs and supports many deployment settings (on-device, low-latency, privacy-constrained). Realizing KD's benefits requires careful choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student capacity, how to obtain or synthesize distillation data, and how to combine KD with complementary compression methods. This paper argues that KD should be treated as the default, composable core of compression pipelines while acknowledging and addressing its practical limitations through principled engineering and evaluation.

papers_seen.author: Alexander
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Context-Sensitive Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and versatile technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, deployable models while preserving much of the teacher's performance. KD has matured into a toolkit that includes soft-target matching, intermediate-feature transfer, multi-teacher schedules, curriculum and data-aware strategies, and domain-specific variants. As a result, KD should be treated as a central element of any production-oriented compression pipeline—but it must be applied with attention to teacher–student capacity alignment, data availability, task requirements, and complementary compression methods to achieve reliable, efficient deployment.

papers_seen.author: Hill
papers_seen.title: A Deep Hierarchical Approach to Lifelong Learning in Minecraft
papers_seen.abstract: We propose a lifelong learning system that has the ability to reuse and transfer knowledge from one task to another while efficiently retaining the previously learned knowledge-base. Knowledge is transferred by learning reusable skills to solve tasks in Minecraft, a popular video game which is an unsolved and high-dimensional lifelong learning problem. These reusable skills, which we refer to as Deep Skill Networks, are then incorporated into our novel Hierarchical Deep Reinforcement Learning Network (H-DRLN) architecture using two techniques: (1) a deep skill array and (2) skill distillation, our novel variation of policy distillation (Rusu et. al. 2015) for learning skills. Skill distillation enables the HDRLN to efficiently retain knowledge and therefore scale in lifelong learning, by accumulating knowledge and encapsulating multiple reusable skills into a single distilled network. The H-DRLN exhibits superior performance and lower learning sample complexity compared to the regular Deep Q Network (Mnih et. al. 2015) in sub-domains of Minecraft.

papers_seen.author: Maldonado
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression have emerged as critical techniques for deploying neural networks in resource-constrained environments. These methods enable the transfer of knowledge from larger teacher models to more compact student models while maintaining predictive performance. Applications span diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and multimodal learning, with approaches ranging from feature-level distillation to collaborative training strategies.

papers_seen.author: Turner
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Applications, and Practical Considerations
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression have become essential techniques for deploying large neural networks efficiently in resource-constrained environments. These methods enable the transfer of knowledge from large, complex teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models while maintaining predictive performance. Knowledge distillation addresses critical real-world deployment constraints including latency, memory consumption, privacy, and device heterogeneity, making it indispensable for practical applications across computer vision, natural language processing, speech recognition, and specialized domains. The field has evolved from simple soft-label matching to a rich toolkit encompassing multiple complementary techniques that can be combined to achieve substantial efficiency gains while retaining most of the teacher model's performance.

papers_seen.author: Williamson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: A Practical and Essential Approach for Efficient Deep Learning and NLP Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and versatile technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, deployable models while maintaining competitive performance. By transferring knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to resource-efficient student networks, distillation enables practical deployment of state-of-the-art systems across diverse domains including natural language processing and computer vision. This paper argues that knowledge distillation should be treated as a central, composable component of compression pipelines that addresses critical constraints in latency, memory efficiency, and computational requirements, though its success depends on careful design choices regarding teacher-student alignment, data strategies, and integration with complementary compression techniques.

papers_seen.author: Perkins
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: An Essential but Context-Aware Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a widely adopted approach for transferring predictive behavior and internal structure from large teacher models to smaller student models. KD enables substantial reductions in model size, inference latency, and resource use while often preserving strong task performance. However, its practical value depends on careful choice of teacher signals, student capacity, data strategies, and complementary compression techniques; when applied thoughtfully, KD supports privacy-preserving, domain-adaptive, and hardware-aware deployment of compact models, but it is not a one-size-fits-all solution and must be integrated into broader compression and robustness workflows.

papers_seen.author: Reese
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Default, Composable Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible framework for producing compact student models that retain much of the performance of larger teacher models. When treated as a design-first tool rather than a single loss term, KD supports a range of mechanisms—soft-target transfer, intermediate-representation matching, multi-teacher and online schemes, and data-aware (including data-free) methods—and composes naturally with pruning, quantization, and architecture-search. However, realizing KD’s benefits in production requires diagnostic attention to teacher–student alignment, data and domain shift, rare-token behavior, and optimization gaps; when those concerns are addressed, KD yields deployment-ready models that meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints across vision, speech, and language tasks.

papers_seen.author: Fowler
papers_seen.title: Less is More: Task-aware Layer-wise Distillation for Language Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Layer-wise distillation is a powerful tool to compress large models (i.e. teacher models) into small ones (i.e., student models). The student distills knowledge from the teacher by mimicking the hidden representations of the teacher at every intermediate layer. However, layer-wise distillation is difficult. Since the student has a smaller model capacity than the teacher, it is often under-fitted. Furthermore, the hidden representations of the teacher contain redundant information that the student does not necessarily need for the target task's learning. To address these challenges, we propose a novel Task-aware layEr-wise Distillation (TED). TED designs task-aware filters to align the hidden representations of the student and the teacher at each layer. The filters select the knowledge that is useful for the target task from the hidden representations. As such, TED reduces the knowledge gap between the two models and helps the student to fit better on the target task. We evaluate TED in two scenarios: continual pre-training and fine-tuning. TED demonstrates significant and consistent improvements over existing distillation methods in both scenarios. Code is available at https://github.com/cliang1453/task-aware-distillation.

papers_seen.author: Lynch
papers_seen.title: Revisiting Knowledge Distillation via Label Smoothing Regularization
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge Distillation (KD) aims to distill the knowledge of a cumbersome teacher model into a lightweight student model. Its success is generally attributed to the privileged information on similarities among categories provided by the teacher model, and in this sense, only strong teacher models are deployed to teach weaker students in practice. In this work, we challenge this common belief by following experimental observations: 1) beyond the acknowledgment that the teacher can improve the student, the student can also enhance the teacher significantly by reversing the KD procedure; 2) a poorly-trained teacher with much lower accuracy than the student can still improve the latter significantly. To explain these observations, we provide a theoretical analysis of the relationships between KD and label smoothing regularization. We prove that 1) KD is a type of learned label smoothing regularization and 2) label smoothing regularization provides a virtual teacher model for KD. From these results, we argue that the success of KD is not fully due to the similarity information between categories from teachers, but also to the regularization of soft targets, which is equally or even more important.   Based on these analyses, we further propose a novel Teacher-free Knowledge Distillation (Tf-KD) framework, where a student model learns from itself or manuallydesigned regularization distribution. The Tf-KD achieves comparable performance with normal KD from a superior teacher, which is well applied when a stronger teacher model is unavailable. Meanwhile, Tf-KD is generic and can be directly deployed for training deep neural networks. Without any extra computation cost, Tf-KD achieves up to 0.65\% improvement on ImageNet over well-established baseline models, which is superior to label smoothing regularization.

papers_seen.author: Baker
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable strategy for compressing large neural models into smaller, efficient students by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations. KD encompasses multiple complementary mechanisms — soft-label supervision, feature- and attention-level imitation, layer-wise alignment, curriculum and meta-learning of teachers, and data-free or privacy-preserving variants — which together enable deployment of high-performing models under latency, memory, and data constraints. Practical success depends on matching distilled signals to student capacity, handling teacher–student architectural mismatches, and addressing robustness and data-availability challenges. This synthesis summarizes prevailing methods, empirical patterns, and practical considerations for KD in vision and NLP settings.

papers_seen.author: Reyes
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core, Contextual Component of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and practically essential approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students while retaining much of teacher performance. KD encompasses multiple transfer targets (soft logits, intermediate representations, attention maps) and protocols (offline, online/self-distillation, multi-teacher), and it is frequently combined with pruning, quantization, and architecture-aware design. However, KD is not a universal silver bullet: its success depends on principled teacher–student alignment, careful selection of transfer signals, data availability or synthesis strategies, and explicit handling of robustness, fairness, and rare behaviors. When treated as the central, composable element within a broader compression pipeline and applied with task- and capacity-aware choices, KD provides a practical default for achieving strong trade-offs between efficiency and performance.

papers_seen.author: Singh
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as an Essential but Context-Aware Framework for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and practical paradigm for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students while largely preserving task performance. KD extends beyond simple logit matching to include feature-level imitation, attention transfer, multi-teacher schemes, data-free variants, and combinations with pruning or quantization. However, realizing KD’s benefits in real systems requires task-aware choices about what to transfer, careful alignment of teacher and student capacities, and strategies for limited or private data; without those design choices, distillation can underperform or propagate undesirable teacher behaviors. This paper argues that KD should be treated as a central, composable tool in model-compression toolkits, applied with principled, data- and optimization-aware practice to achieve robust, efficient deployment.

papers_seen.author: Gordon
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a fundamental model compression technique that enables efficient deployment of large neural networks by transferring knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to smaller, resource-constrained student models. This approach has become essential across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, machine translation, and speech recognition, addressing critical challenges of reducing model size, inference latency, and computational cost while maintaining competitive performance. The field has evolved from simple soft-target matching to sophisticated multi-faceted methodologies encompassing intermediate representation transfer, feature-level distillation, multi-teacher strategies, and data-free approaches. Practical success requires careful orchestration of design choices including teacher-student capacity alignment, selection of appropriate distillation objectives, data availability, and integration with complementary compression techniques.

papers_seen.author: Hancock
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Essential Techniques for Practical Deep Learning Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and versatile technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. By enabling the transfer of knowledge from computationally expensive teacher models to resource-constrained student models, this approach addresses critical deployment challenges across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and specialized applications. The technique encompasses multiple complementary methodologies ranging from soft-label matching to intermediate representation alignment, enabling practical deployment while maintaining accuracy.

papers_seen.author: Jordan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Practice, and Open Challenges
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-capacity teacher models into smaller, efficient student models by transferring information beyond hard labels. A broad family of KD techniques has been developed — including soft-target (logits) matching, intermediate representation and attention mimicry, relational objectives, multi-teacher and online schemes, and data-aware or data-free variants — and KD is routinely combined with complementary compression methods such as pruning, quantization, and architecture search. In practice, KD enables deployment of effective models under latency, memory, and privacy constraints across NLP and other domains, but its success depends on choices about distilled signals, teacher–student capacity alignment, data availability and quality, and evaluation for robustness and distributional shift. Ongoing challenges include automating design choices, preserving robustness and fairness, handling private or absent data, and diagnosing teacher-student mismatch.

papers_seen.author: Bernard
papers_seen.title: Reinforced Multi-Teacher Selection for Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: In natural language processing (NLP) tasks, slow inference speed and huge footprints in GPU usage remain the bottleneck of applying pre-trained deep models in production. As a popular method for model compression, knowledge distillation transfers knowledge from one or multiple large (teacher) models to a small (student) model. When multiple teacher models are available in distillation, the state-of-the-art methods assign a fixed weight to a teacher model in the whole distillation. Furthermore, most of the existing methods allocate an equal weight to every teacher model. In this paper, we observe that, due to the complexity of training examples and the differences in student model capability, learning differentially from teacher models can lead to better performance of student models distilled. We systematically develop a reinforced method to dynamically assign weights to teacher models for different training instances and optimize the performance of student model. Our extensive experimental results on several NLP tasks clearly verify the feasibility and effectiveness of our approach.

papers_seen.author: Harrell
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Applications, and Open Challenges
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model compression techniques transform large, costly models into smaller, faster, or more private models while retaining much of the original performance. Across modalities and tasks, distillation has been applied to compress vision and language models, transfer cross-modal or privileged information, enable deployment under latency and memory constraints, and preserve privacy in distributed settings. Key directions include distillation of logits (soft labels), feature- or attention-level distillation, self-distillation, data-free or zero-shot approaches, and architecture-aware compression. Empirical results show that when carefully designed—often combining distillation with pruning or architecture search—student models can approach teacher accuracy, gain robustness, or enable capabilities (e.g., multimodal generation) previously unavailable to the smaller model. Important open problems remain in data heterogeneity, robustness transfer, and principled teacher-student design for diverse deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Parsons
papers_seen.title: Curriculum Learning for Dense Retrieval Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Recent work has shown that more effective dense retrieval models can be obtained by distilling ranking knowledge from an existing base re-ranking model. In this paper, we propose a generic curriculum learning based optimization framework called CL-DRD that controls the difficulty level of training data produced by the re-ranking (teacher) model. CL-DRD iteratively optimizes the dense retrieval (student) model by increasing the difficulty of the knowledge distillation data made available to it. In more detail, we initially provide the student model coarse-grained preference pairs between documents in the teacher's ranking and progressively move towards finer-grained pairwise document ordering requirements. In our experiments, we apply a simple implementation of the CL-DRD framework to enhance two state-of-the-art dense retrieval models. Experiments on three public passage retrieval datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of our proposed framework.

papers_seen.author: Rogers
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Essential Techniques for Deploying Deep Learning Models
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression have emerged as critical techniques for enabling the deployment of large, powerful deep learning models in resource-constrained environments. By transferring knowledge from larger teacher models to smaller student models, these methods address the fundamental challenge of making state-of-the-art models practical for real-world applications that require fast inference and limited computational resources.

papers_seen.author: Mckee
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable model-compression paradigm that transfers behavior from larger teacher models to smaller student models to reduce memory, latency, and compute while preserving task performance. Over the past decade KD has expanded beyond matching soft-output logits to include intermediate-feature and layer-level matching, multi-teacher and many-to-many mappings, data-free and privacy-aware approaches, and hybrid pipelines that combine distillation with pruning, quantization, and architecture search. Empirical work shows distilled students can often approach teacher performance across vision, language, graph, and retrieval tasks, but practical success depends on choices about what is transferred, how teachers and students are matched, and how limited or private data are handled. Key open problems include principled teacher selection, coping with data heterogeneity or absence, robustness to rare phenomena and bias transfer, and tighter theoretical understanding of when distillation improves generalization.

papers_seen.author: Wood
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-capacity models into smaller, efficient students by transferring predictive behavior, intermediate representations, or synthetic training signals. Across modalities and tasks, KD has become a central practical technique for reducing inference cost, memory footprint, and latency while often preserving much of the teacher’s performance. Its value is greatest when combined with complementary compression methods and when distillation objectives, data strategies, and teacher–student capacity are chosen to match deployment constraints. Remaining challenges include handling absent or private data, transferring robustness and fairness properties, and diagnosing teacher–student mismatch, which motivate ongoing method and evaluation work.

papers_seen.author: Mason
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Comprehensive Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression have become essential techniques for deploying large neural networks in resource-constrained environments. These approaches enable the transfer of knowledge from large, high-capacity teacher models to smaller, efficient student models, achieving substantial reductions in parameters, memory consumption, and inference latency while maintaining competitive accuracy. The field encompasses diverse methodologies and has been successfully applied across computer vision, natural language processing, speech recognition, and other domains. Practical success requires careful design choices regarding what signals to transfer, how to align teacher-student architectures, and how to manage data availability and privacy constraints.

papers_seen.author: Lopez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Essential Default Strategy for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and versatile technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, deployable student models while maintaining competitive performance. By transferring knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to resource-constrained student networks, knowledge distillation enables practical deployment across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, and specialized applications. The technique encompasses multiple complementary mechanisms and can be strategically combined with pruning, quantization, and architecture search. However, its effectiveness depends critically on careful design choices regarding teacher-student alignment, signal selection, data availability, and task-specific adaptation. This paper argues that knowledge distillation should serve as the default starting point for model compression in modern deep learning and NLP systems, provided it is paired with principled design workflows and comprehensive evaluation strategies.

papers_seen.author: Bright
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Critical Technique for Deep Learning Model Compression and NLP Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for compressing large deep learning models while maintaining performance. This approach transfers knowledge from computationally expensive teacher models to lightweight student models, enabling efficient deployment across diverse applications. This paper argues that knowledge distillation represents an essential strategy for addressing the trade-off between model complexity and practical deployment requirements in both computer vision and natural language processing domains.

papers_seen.author: Wolf
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Core Mechanisms and Practical Applications
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a fundamental technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, deployable student models while maintaining competitive performance. By transferring knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to resource-constrained students, knowledge distillation enables efficient deployment across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, and specialized applications. The approach encompasses multiple methodologies, from soft-target matching to intermediate-feature alignment, and addresses critical deployment challenges including model size reduction, inference latency, memory efficiency, and computational cost. Practical success depends on careful design choices, teacher-student alignment, data availability, and integration with complementary compression techniques.

papers_seen.author: Hoffman
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Task-Aware Approach to Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) provides a flexible framework to transfer predictive behavior and internal representations from large, costly models (teachers) to smaller, faster models (students). Across modalities and tasks, KD can both preserve or even improve accuracy while enabling deployment constraints such as lower latency, reduced memory, quantized arithmetic, and multi-task or privacy-aware settings. Realizing these benefits requires matching the distillation strategy to task structure and student capacity: approaches that exploit multi-teacher signals, task-aware layer alignment, teacher adaptation, or self-distillation consistently produce better compressed models. I argue that distillation is not a single recipe but a family of practical, complementary techniques that — when chosen and combined thoughtfully — make state-of-the-art models usable in resource-constrained and application-specific scenarios.

papers_seen.author: Dunn
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical Core Strategy for Deep Learning and NLP Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and indispensable technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, efficient student models while maintaining competitive performance. By transferring knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to resource-constrained student networks, knowledge distillation enables deployment of state-of-the-art deep learning and NLP systems in practically constrained environments. The approach encompasses diverse methodologies ranging from simple soft-target matching to sophisticated intermediate representation alignment, and when combined with complementary compression techniques, represents the core strategy for reliable and practical neural network deployment across multiple domains.

papers_seen.author: Moore
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical, Context-Sensitive Default for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible family of methods for transferring behavior from large teacher models to smaller student models to reduce inference cost while retaining much of task performance. KD is most effective when treated as a configurable toolkit—selecting what to transfer (logits, features, attention, etc.), matching teacher and student capacity, and combining distillation with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture changes). Practical deployment also requires attention to data availability (including synthesized or data-free approaches), privacy constraints, and robustness under distribution shift. When applied with these caveats, KD routinely yields deployable models that meet real-world latency, memory, and privacy requirements.

papers_seen.author: Lynch
papers_seen.title: Cross-modal Knowledge Distillation for Vision-to-Sensor Action Recognition
papers_seen.abstract: Human activity recognition (HAR) based on multi-modal approach has been recently shown to improve the accuracy performance of HAR. However, restricted computational resources associated with wearable devices, i.e., smartwatch, failed to directly support such advanced methods. To tackle this issue, this study introduces an end-to-end Vision-to-Sensor Knowledge Distillation (VSKD) framework. In this VSKD framework, only time-series data, i.e., accelerometer data, is needed from wearable devices during the testing phase. Therefore, this framework will not only reduce the computational demands on edge devices, but also produce a learning model that closely matches the performance of the computational expensive multi-modal approach. In order to retain the local temporal relationship and facilitate visual deep learning models, we first convert time-series data to two-dimensional images by applying the Gramian Angular Field ( GAF) based encoding method. We adopted ResNet18 and multi-scale TRN with BN-Inception as teacher and student network in this study, respectively. A novel loss function, named Distance and Angle-wised Semantic Knowledge loss (DASK), is proposed to mitigate the modality variations between the vision and the sensor domain. Extensive experimental results on UTD-MHAD, MMAct, and Berkeley-MHAD datasets demonstrate the effectiveness and competitiveness of the proposed VSKD model which can deployed on wearable sensors.

papers_seen.author: Rocha
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and Natural Language Processing
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a fundamental technique for compressing neural networks by transferring knowledge from large teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models. This approach has become increasingly important for deploying sophisticated deep learning systems in resource-constrained environments while maintaining competitive performance. Applications span multiple domains including computer vision, natural language processing, graph neural networks, and specialized tasks such as pose estimation and scene understanding. Recent advances have extended distillation beyond basic teacher-student frameworks to encompass data augmentation strategies, multi-teacher selection, and zero-shot learning scenarios where original training data is unavailable.

papers_seen.author: Gallegos
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Core Mechanisms and Practical Applications
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and widely-adopted technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, efficient models while preserving competitive performance. This approach transfers knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to resource-constrained student networks, enabling practical deployment of sophisticated deep learning and natural language processing systems across diverse applications. Knowledge distillation encompasses multiple complementary mechanisms and strategies, and when properly designed and combined with other compression techniques, provides substantial reductions in model size, computational cost, and inference latency without significant accuracy loss.

papers_seen.author: Peterson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Practical and Versatile Strategy for Deep Learning Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach transfers knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to lightweight student models, enabling practical deployment in resource-constrained environments. While knowledge distillation is widely applicable across diverse domains including computer vision and natural language processing, its effectiveness depends critically on careful design choices, appropriate teacher-student alignment, and thoughtful integration with complementary compression techniques.

papers_seen.author: Villegas
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Applications, and Practical Considerations
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and model compression have emerged as fundamental techniques for transferring knowledge from large, high-capacity teacher neural networks to smaller, more efficient student models. These methods address critical practical deployment constraints including inference latency, memory consumption, computational efficiency, and device heterogeneity while maintaining competitive performance. KD encompasses diverse methodologies spanning output-level soft-target matching, intermediate feature and layer-level alignment, relational and attention-based transfers, and can be combined with complementary compression techniques such as pruning, quantization, and neural architecture search. The field encompasses broad applications across computer vision, natural language processing, machine translation, speech recognition, and specialized domains, establishing KD as a versatile and practical toolkit for enabling efficient model deployment in resource-constrained environments.

papers_seen.author: Conner
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Context‑Aware Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. When applied with task- and deployment-aware choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student capacities, and how to handle limited or private data, KD yields substantial gains in size, latency, and efficiency while preserving much of teacher performance. However, distillation is not a one-size-fits-all solution: its success depends on careful selection of distilled signals, complementary structural compression techniques, and rigorous evaluation under domain shift, rare-event behavior, and fairness constraints.

papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Techniques, Applications, and Design Principles
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a fundamental and versatile technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, efficient student models by transferring knowledge from high-capacity teacher models. This approach enables practical deployment of state-of-the-art deep learning systems in resource-constrained environments across domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and specialized applications. Knowledge distillation encompasses multiple methodologies and transfer mechanisms, and is most effective when combined with complementary compression techniques and careful consideration of teacher-student alignment, data availability, and task-specific requirements.

papers_seen.author: Cannon
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, powerful models into smaller, faster models by transferring information beyond hard labels. In NLP and broader deep learning, KD has been applied to pre-trained transformers, sequence models, ensembles, and cross-modal architectures using techniques that include soft-label matching, intermediate feature supervision, progressive module replacement, architecture search, data augmentation, and adversarial sample selection. These methods trade off fidelity to the teacher, student capacity, and inference efficiency; recent work emphasizes task-adaptive compression, improved feature alignment, and tailoring teachers to be more 'student-friendly' to maximize transfer. Empirical results show that carefully designed KD procedures can retain much of the teacher's performance while reducing model size and latency, enabling deployment in resource-constrained settings.

papers_seen.author: Garcia
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large neural models into smaller, deployable students by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations. A diverse array of distillation mechanisms—matching soft logits, feature- and attention-level mimicry, layer- and module-level mappings, multi-teacher fusion, and synthetic-data or data-free strategies—has been developed to address deployment constraints such as latency, memory, privacy, and heterogeneous device capacities. Practical pipelines combine these mechanisms with task- and architecture-aware choices to retain teacher capabilities while meeting real-world constraints. This synthesis summarizes central methods, empirical findings, system-level approaches, and recurring practical recommendations drawn from recent work.

papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Context-Sensitive Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and versatile technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, deployable models while preserving much of the teacher's performance. KD has matured into a toolkit that includes soft-target matching, intermediate-feature transfer, multi-teacher schedules, curriculum and data-aware strategies, and domain-specific variants. As a result, KD should be treated as a central element of any production-oriented compression pipeline—but it must be applied with attention to teacher–student capacity alignment, data availability, task requirements, and complementary compression methods to achieve reliable, efficient deployment.

Practical success depends on careful design choices including teacher-student capacity alignment, selection of appropriate distillation objectives, management of data availability, and explicit attention to robustness and fairness considerations.

papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as an Essential Strategy for Neural Network Compression: Mechanisms, Applications, and Practical Design Principles
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and versatile approach for compressing large neural networks into smaller, efficient student models suitable for deployment in resource-constrained environments. By transferring knowledge from high-capacity teacher models through diverse mechanisms—ranging from soft-target matching to intermediate representation alignment—knowledge distillation enables substantial reductions in model size and computational cost while maintaining competitive performance. This paper argues that knowledge distillation, when combined with complementary compression techniques and careful task-aware design choices, represents an indispensable tool for bringing state-of-the-art deep learning models into practical systems across computer vision and natural language processing domains.

papers_seen.author: Ellis
papers_seen.title: On Representation Knowledge Distillation for Graph Neural Networks
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a learning paradigm for boosting resource-efficient graph neural networks (GNNs) using more expressive yet cumbersome teacher models. Past work on distillation for GNNs proposed the Local Structure Preserving loss (LSP), which matches local structural relationships defined over edges across the student and teacher's node embeddings. This paper studies whether preserving the global topology of how the teacher embeds graph data can be a more effective distillation objective for GNNs, as real-world graphs often contain latent interactions and noisy edges. We propose Graph Contrastive Representation Distillation (G-CRD), which uses contrastive learning to implicitly preserve global topology by aligning the student node embeddings to those of the teacher in a shared representation space. Additionally, we introduce an expanded set of benchmarks on large-scale real-world datasets where the performance gap between teacher and student GNNs is non-negligible. Experiments across 4 datasets and 14 heterogeneous GNN architectures show that G-CRD consistently boosts the performance and robustness of lightweight GNNs, outperforming LSP (and a global structure preserving variant of LSP) as well as baselines from 2D computer vision. An analysis of the representational similarity among teacher and student embedding spaces reveals that G-CRD balances preserving local and global relationships, while structure preserving approaches are best at preserving one or the other. Our code is available at https://github.com/chaitjo/efficient-gnns

papers_seen.author: Hayden
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: A Versatile Yet Contextually Dependent Approach to Efficient Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and versatile technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient student models while preserving competitive performance. By transferring knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to resource-constrained students, this approach addresses critical deployment challenges including computational cost, latency, memory consumption, and inference efficiency across domains such as computer vision and natural language processing. However, the effectiveness of knowledge distillation depends critically on careful design choices, contextual application strategies, and combination with complementary compression methods.

papers_seen.author: Hayes
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Applications, and Practical Strategies
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a fundamental technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient student models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach transfers knowledge from complex teacher models to resource-constrained students, enabling practical deployment of state-of-the-art systems across computer vision, natural language processing, and specialized domains. By addressing critical constraints of latency, memory efficiency, and computational cost, knowledge distillation has become essential for making sophisticated deep learning models practical for real-world applications.

papers_seen.author: Collins
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Principles, Methods, and Applications
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and model compression represent a broad set of techniques for transferring knowledge from larger, more complex neural networks to smaller, more efficient models. These approaches enable deployment of high-performing deep learning systems in resource-constrained environments while maintaining competitive accuracy. Applications span diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, machine translation, speech recognition, and graph neural networks. Knowledge distillation has evolved from a heuristic compression technique to a versatile, modality-agnostic toolkit that addresses critical challenges in model efficiency, latency reduction, privacy preservation, and task-specific performance optimization.

papers_seen.author: Miranda
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Applications, and Practical Considerations
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a fundamental technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, efficient student models suitable for deployment in resource-constrained environments. By transferring predictive behavior and representational knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to compact students, knowledge distillation enables substantial reductions in model size, inference latency, and computational cost while maintaining competitive performance. The field encompasses diverse methodologies, complementary compression techniques, and applications across computer vision, natural language processing, speech recognition, and other domains. Effective deployment requires careful design choices regarding what knowledge to transfer, teacher-student alignment, data strategies, and integration with complementary compression approaches.

papers_seen.author: Hicks
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful technique for model compression and knowledge transfer in deep learning and NLP applications. By enabling the transfer of knowledge from large teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models, knowledge distillation addresses critical challenges of inference speed, memory consumption, and computational resource requirements. This approach has been successfully applied across diverse domains including NLP tasks, computer vision, federated learning, and various specialized applications, offering practical solutions for deploying complex models in resource-constrained environments.

papers_seen.author: Potts
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning: Necessity, Methods, and Practical Limitations
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a central technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, deployable models while maintaining competitive performance. By transferring knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to resource-constrained student networks, KD addresses critical challenges in deploying sophisticated deep learning systems across diverse domains. This position argues that while KD is an essential and versatile tool that should be adopted as a foundational component of modern compression pipelines, its effectiveness depends critically on careful task-aware design, proper teacher-student alignment, thoughtful data strategies, and integration with complementary compression methods. KD is not a universal solution but rather a practical framework that must be wielded deliberately to navigate real-world deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Orr
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Comprehensive Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a fundamental model compression technique that transfers knowledge from large, high-capacity teacher networks to smaller, more efficient student networks. This approach enables the practical deployment of state-of-the-art deep learning systems in resource-constrained environments while maintaining competitive performance. Knowledge distillation addresses critical real-world challenges including computational efficiency, memory constraints, inference latency, privacy preservation, and device heterogeneity. The technique has been successfully applied across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, speech recognition, and multimodal learning, demonstrating its versatility and essential role in practical neural network deployment.

papers_seen.author: Bennett
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Applications, and Practical Insights
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a fundamental model compression technique that enables the transfer of knowledge from large, high-capacity teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models. This approach addresses critical deployment constraints including latency, memory consumption, computational cost, and privacy concerns, making state-of-the-art neural networks practical for resource-constrained environments. Knowledge distillation has evolved into a versatile toolkit encompassing diverse methodologies and is widely applied across computer vision, natural language processing, machine translation, speech recognition, and specialized domains. While KD routinely produces favorable efficiency-accuracy tradeoffs, its practical success depends on careful task-aware design, appropriate handling of data regimes, and integration with complementary compression techniques.

papers_seen.author: Francis
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Essential Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and versatile technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. By transferring knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to resource-constrained student models, knowledge distillation addresses critical deployment challenges including reduced latency, memory footprint, and computational cost across diverse domains such as computer vision, natural language processing, machine translation, and speech recognition. However, effective distillation requires careful orchestration of multiple design choices, including the selection of distillation targets, teacher-student capacity alignment, data strategies, and integration with complementary compression techniques to achieve reliable results.

papers_seen.author: Chapman
papers_seen.title: What is Known About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly adopted family of techniques for compressing large teacher models into smaller, efficient student models by transferring predictive behavior, intermediate representations, or synthesized training signals. KD is applied across modalities and tasks to reduce model size, latency, and energy while retaining much of the original performance. Successful application of KD typically treats it as a composable component of a broader compression pipeline (together with pruning, quantization, and architecture search), adapts the choice of distilled signal to task and data constraints, and evaluates students under realistic distribution shift and deployment requirements. Important open issues include preserving robustness, fairness and rare-behavior transfer, operating without original training data, and principled teacher–student architecture alignment.

papers_seen.author: Riley
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and versatile technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, deployable student models while maintaining competitive performance. By transferring knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to resource-constrained students, this approach enables significant reductions in model size, memory requirements, and inference latency across diverse domains including computer vision and natural language processing. The field has evolved from simple output-level soft-label matching to a comprehensive toolkit encompassing feature-level alignment, multi-teacher strategies, and integration with complementary compression methods, with practical success depending on careful design choices regarding distillation targets, teacher-student alignment, and data strategies.

papers_seen.author: Jackson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning: Methods, Applications, and Empirical Insights
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a widely adopted technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models by transferring knowledge from a teacher network to a student network. This approach has become increasingly important for deploying deep learning models in resource-constrained environments such as mobile and edge devices. The field encompasses diverse methodologies ranging from feature-level distillation to cross-modal approaches, with applications spanning computer vision, natural language processing, and multimodal learning. Recent research has advanced both theoretical understanding and practical implementations of knowledge distillation, demonstrating significant improvements in model compression while maintaining predictive performance.

papers_seen.author: Burke
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Composable, but Limited Toolkit for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students by transferring information beyond hard labels. KD routinely yields substantial reductions in inference cost, memory footprint, and latency while preserving much of teacher performance across vision and language tasks. However, its practical success hinges on task-aware design, data strategies, and complementary compression methods; it is a powerful tool but not a universal solution. This paper argues that KD should be treated as a foundational and composable component of compression pipelines, paired with principled choices about targets, architectures, and training regimes to maximize utility while acknowledging optimization and data-driven limits.

papers_seen.author: Lindsey
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Essential Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as the primary and most practical approach for compressing large neural networks into smaller, deployable student models while maintaining competitive performance. By transferring knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to resource-constrained students, knowledge distillation enables efficient deployment across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, and specialized applications. This paper argues that knowledge distillation should serve as the default compression strategy when properly combined with complementary techniques and carefully designed to address real-world deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Hayes
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Applications, and Practical Considerations
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models suitable for deployment in resource-constrained environments. This approach enables the transfer of knowledge from large, complex teacher models to compact student models through multiple mechanisms including soft-target matching, intermediate representation alignment, and relational constraints. Knowledge distillation addresses critical challenges in deploying deep learning systems across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and multimodal applications, providing practical pathways for creating efficient models while maintaining competitive performance.

papers_seen.author: Garcia
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Critical Approach to Model Compression in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful technique for compressing neural networks by transferring knowledge from large teacher models to smaller student models. This approach enables efficient deployment of state-of-the-art models on resource-constrained devices while maintaining performance. The technique has proven effective across multiple domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and graph neural networks. This paper argues that knowledge distillation represents a pragmatic and essential strategy for bridging the gap between model performance and computational efficiency in modern deep learning systems.

papers_seen.author: Camacho
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: Essential, Composable, and Context-Sensitive for Practical Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations. KD supports multiple transfer signals (soft targets, intermediate features, relational structure) and protocols (offline, online, multi-teacher, data-free) and is most effective when integrated with complementary compression methods and matched to deployment constraints. While KD routinely offers strong size–performance trade-offs, realizing those gains in practice requires task- and data-aware design, careful teacher–student alignment, and evaluation for robustness and undesirable behavior.

papers_seen.author: Robinson
papers_seen.title: Towards Understanding Ensemble, Knowledge Distillation and Self-Distillation in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: We formally study how ensemble of deep learning models can improve test accuracy, and how the superior performance of ensemble can be distilled into a single model using knowledge distillation. We consider the challenging case where the ensemble is simply an average of the outputs of a few independently trained neural networks with the SAME architecture, trained using the SAME algorithm on the SAME data set, and they only differ by the random seeds used in the initialization.   We show that ensemble/knowledge distillation in Deep Learning works very differently from traditional learning theory (such as boosting or NTKs, neural tangent kernels). To properly understand them, we develop a theory showing that when data has a structure we refer to as ``multi-view'', then ensemble of independently trained neural networks can provably improve test accuracy, and such superior test accuracy can also be provably distilled into a single model by training a single model to match the output of the ensemble instead of the true label. Our result sheds light on how ensemble works in deep learning in a way that is completely different from traditional theorems, and how the ``dark knowledge'' is hidden in the outputs of the ensemble and can be used in distillation. In the end, we prove that self-distillation can also be viewed as implicitly combining ensemble and knowledge distillation to improve test accuracy.
