papers_seen.author: Flynn
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: A Critical Strategy for Practical Deep Learning Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as an essential technique for deploying large neural networks in resource-constrained environments by transferring knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models. This approach enables substantial reductions in model size, computational cost, and inference latency while maintaining competitive predictive performance. While knowledge distillation is not a universal solution, when carefully combined with complementary strategies such as representation-level transfer, task-specific optimization, and data-aware techniques, it becomes an indispensable tool for bringing state-of-the-art deep learning and NLP models into practical systems across diverse domains.

papers_seen.author: Hoffman
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Task-Aware Approach to Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) provides a flexible framework to transfer predictive behavior and internal representations from large, costly models (teachers) to smaller, faster models (students). Across modalities and tasks, KD can both preserve or even improve accuracy while enabling deployment constraints such as lower latency, reduced memory, quantized arithmetic, and multi-task or privacy-aware settings. Realizing these benefits requires matching the distillation strategy to task structure and student capacity: approaches that exploit multi-teacher signals, task-aware layer alignment, teacher adaptation, or self-distillation consistently produce better compressed models. I argue that distillation is not a single recipe but a family of practical, complementary techniques that — when chosen and combined thoughtfully — make state-of-the-art models usable in resource-constrained and application-specific scenarios.

papers_seen.author: Beck
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core but Contextual Tool for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, broadly applicable approach for producing smaller, faster models from large teachers. When combined with complementary methods—careful pretraining of compact architectures, feature-level and layer-aware objectives, multi-teacher or meta-learned teachers, and data-aware or data-free procedures—KD routinely yields deployable models that meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints. At the same time, KD has important empirical and theoretical limits tied to data availability, teacher–student mismatch, and optimization dynamics, so it should be embedded in a broader compression strategy rather than treated as a universal cure-all.

papers_seen.author: Lewis
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Contemporary Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-performing teacher models into smaller student models by transferring soft outputs, intermediate representations, or behavioral constraints. KD is applied across vision, language, speech, and specialized tasks to reduce latency, memory use, and energy while often preserving most of the teacher’s performance. Effective distillation depends on choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student capacities, available data (including data-free or synthetic approaches), and integration with complementary techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search). Practical deployment requires task-aware design, careful evaluation of trade-offs (accuracy, robustness, privacy), and ongoing work toward automated, domain-adaptive, and privacy-preserving pipelines.

papers_seen.author: Rivera
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Cornerstone of Practical Model Compression: A Unified Framework for Efficient Deep Learning Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation represents a fundamental and versatile approach to compressing large neural networks into smaller, deployable student models while maintaining competitive performance. By transferring knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to resource-constrained students through multiple complementary mechanisms, knowledge distillation enables efficient inference across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, and speech recognition. This position argues that knowledge distillation should be treated as the central, composable framework of any practical model compression strategy, supported by extensive empirical validation, diverse methodologies, and practical deployment considerations across multiple modalities.

papers_seen.author: Hale
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core Strategy for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a versatile and essential technique for compressing large neural models into smaller, efficient student networks suitable for deployment in resource-constrained environments. By transferring knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to lightweight student networks, knowledge distillation enables significant reductions in model size, latency, and memory consumption while maintaining competitive performance across diverse domains. However, its effectiveness depends critically on careful design choices, matching distillation objectives to student capacity, and integration with complementary compression techniques to ensure robust, production-ready results.

papers_seen.author: Stanley
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central Framework for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and versatile technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, deployable student models while maintaining competitive performance. This paper argues that knowledge distillation should be treated as a central, composable framework for model compression across deep learning and NLP domains. While offering substantial benefits in reducing model size, latency, and memory requirements, knowledge distillation's practical success depends on careful design choices, complementary compression techniques, and thoughtful consideration of its inherent limitations.

papers_seen.author: Lynch
papers_seen.title: The Case for Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Multifaceted Tool for Model Compression and Transfer
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has matured from a single-purpose compression trick into a flexible framework that can compress models, transfer inductive biases, improve fairness and domain adaptability, and support continual learning across modalities. Its strengths come from multiple instantiations—logit matching, feature mimicking, contrastive representation alignment, module replacement, and automated search guided by distillation—which together make it broadly applicable for deploying high-performing models under resource constraints. At the same time, careful choice of distillation targets, mixture with hard labels, and awareness of teacher imperfections are key to realizing its benefits in practice.

papers_seen.author: Lane
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a fundamental technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, deployable student models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach transfers knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to resource-constrained student networks, enabling practical deployment in latency-, memory-, and energy-limited environments across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, and multimodal systems. The technique encompasses multiple transfer mechanisms and methodologies, with success depending on careful design choices regarding what knowledge to transfer, teacher-student alignment, and integration with complementary compression techniques.

papers_seen.author: Moreno
papers_seen.title: Promises and Practicalities of Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable strategy for compressing large models into smaller, faster students while preserving performance. Empirical successes span vision, language, graph, and retrieval tasks, and variants include multi-teacher, self-distillation, feature-level and adversarial formulations. However, distillation is not a panacea: its benefits depend on how knowledge is represented (soft targets vs. internal features), on the student–teacher interaction mechanisms, and on data- and deployment-specific constraints (e.g., heterogeneous clients or low-frequency tokens). This article argues that KD is a powerful and flexible tool when combined with principled modifications — such as internal-representation distillation, projector ensembles, multi-teacher curricula, improved data augmentation, and task-aware distillation losses — but that practitioners must attend to these factors to realize reliable compression and generalization gains.

papers_seen.author: Dudley
papers_seen.title: Attention-Guided Answer Distillation for Machine Reading Comprehension
papers_seen.abstract: Despite that current reading comprehension systems have achieved significant advancements, their promising performances are often obtained at the cost of making an ensemble of numerous models. Besides, existing approaches are also vulnerable to adversarial attacks. This paper tackles these problems by leveraging knowledge distillation, which aims to transfer knowledge from an ensemble model to a single model. We first demonstrate that vanilla knowledge distillation applied to answer span prediction is effective for reading comprehension systems. We then propose two novel approaches that not only penalize the prediction on confusing answers but also guide the training with alignment information distilled from the ensemble. Experiments show that our best student model has only a slight drop of 0.4% F1 on the SQuAD test set compared to the ensemble teacher, while running 12x faster during inference. It even outperforms the teacher on adversarial SQuAD datasets and NarrativeQA benchmark.

papers_seen.author: Burton
papers_seen.title: Efficient Transformer-based Large Scale Language Representations using Hardware-friendly Block Structured Pruning
papers_seen.abstract: Pre-trained large-scale language models have increasingly demonstrated high accuracy on many natural language processing (NLP) tasks. However, the limited weight storage and computational speed on hardware platforms have impeded the popularity of pre-trained models, especially in the era of edge computing. In this work, we propose an efficient transformer-based large-scale language representation using hardware-friendly block structure pruning. We incorporate the reweighted group Lasso into block-structured pruning for optimization. Besides the significantly reduced weight storage and computation, the proposed approach achieves high compression rates. Experimental results on different models (BERT, RoBERTa, and DistilBERT) on the General Language Understanding Evaluation (GLUE) benchmark tasks show that we achieve up to 5.0x with zero or minor accuracy degradation on certain task(s). Our proposed method is also orthogonal to existing compact pre-trained language models such as DistilBERT using knowledge distillation, since a further 1.79x average compression rate can be achieved on top of DistilBERT with zero or minor accuracy degradation. It is suitable to deploy the final compressed model on resource-constrained edge devices.

papers_seen.author: Larson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and practical technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, efficient student models suitable for deployment in resource-constrained environments. This approach transfers knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to compact student networks through multiple mechanisms, enabling significant reductions in computational requirements, memory footprint, and inference latency while maintaining competitive performance. Knowledge distillation has proven broadly applicable across diverse domains and can be effectively combined with complementary compression techniques to achieve practical deployment of state-of-the-art deep learning and NLP systems.

papers_seen.author: Hill
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Comprehensive Overview
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and versatile technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient student models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach transfers knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to resource-constrained student networks, enabling practical deployment across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, machine translation, and specialized applications. The field encompasses multiple complementary mechanisms and methodologies, ranging from soft-target matching to intermediate representation alignment, with effectiveness depending on careful design choices regarding teacher-student coupling, data availability, and task-specific adaptation.

papers_seen.author: Novak
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Comprehensive Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a central technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while preserving performance. This method transfers knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to lower-capacity student models, enabling deployment of state-of-the-art deep learning systems on resource-constrained devices. The approach has been successfully applied across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, speech processing, and graph neural networks, with various methodological innovations continuously expanding its scope and effectiveness.

papers_seen.author: Henry
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Default for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP (with Design Caveats)
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a proven, versatile technique for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students while preserving much of teacher performance. KD supports multiple transfer mechanisms (soft targets, representation alignment, relational and layer-wise objectives) and integrates well with complementary compression steps, enabling substantial reductions in inference latency and footprint for NLP and other domains. However, realizing these gains reliably requires careful choices about distillation targets, teacher–student capacity alignment, handling scarce or private data, multi-teacher coordination, and robustness under distribution shift. When applied with task-aware design and complementary methods, KD should be treated as the practical default for model compression, not as a black-box panacea.

papers_seen.author: Foster
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Central, Flexible Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, empirically effective framework for producing compact models that retain much of the performance of larger teachers. KD variants—ranging from logits matching to internal-feature alignment, adversarial/sample-synthesis methods, multi-teacher and online schemes, and privacy-aware protocols—enable practitioners to trade off model size, latency, privacy, and deployment constraints. Realizing these benefits in practice requires careful choices about what signals to transfer, how to align teacher and student representations, and how to handle data constraints such as privacy or unavailability. When integrated with complementary techniques (data synthesis, layer mapping, selective sampling, and curriculum designs) KD consistently yields practical compressed models across vision, language, graphs, and multimodal tasks.

papers_seen.author: Stewart
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: A Practical and Necessary Approach for Efficient Deep Learning Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and versatile technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. By transferring knowledge from computationally expensive teacher models to resource-constrained student models, this approach enables practical deployment of state-of-the-art deep learning and NLP systems across diverse applications. The technique encompasses multiple complementary methodologies and is most effective when carefully designed and combined with other compression strategies to address real-world deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Gibson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Mechanisms, Practice, and Open Problems
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses high-capacity teacher models into smaller student models by transferring predictive behavior and internal structure. Across vision and language, distillation methods span softened-output matching, intermediate representation and attention alignment, self-distillation, multi-teacher schedules, and data-side interventions such as augmentation or synthetic data. In practice, distillation is combined with pruning, quantization, and architecture-aware design to meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints; its success depends on choices about distilled targets, teacher–student capacity alignment, and data availability. Open challenges include reliable transfer of low-frequency and structural knowledge, operation without original training data, mitigating transfer of undesirable behaviors, and automating teacher–student design for task-specific compression.

papers_seen.author: Jennings
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Practical Model Compression: Essential but Context‑Dependent
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a pragmatic approach for compressing large neural networks into smaller, deployable models by transferring knowledge from high‑capacity teacher models to lightweight students. KD yields strong practical gains in latency, memory, and energy efficiency across vision and NLP when combined with task‑aware choices about what to distill, how to prepare teachers and students, and which complementary compression tools to apply. However, its effectiveness depends on data regime, teacher–student capacity alignment, the choice of distilled signals, and careful attention to robustness and bias transfer. KD should therefore be treated as a central element of model‑compression toolkits, applied thoughtfully and evaluated under deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Campbell
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has become a central, practical approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students across deep learning and NLP. KD encompasses multiple mechanisms (soft-target matching, intermediate-feature imitation, attention and relation transfer), a variety of operational modes (multi-teacher, data-free, online, federated), and often works best when combined with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search). While KD routinely yields strong size–performance tradeoffs for real-world deployment, open challenges remain in teacher–student design, robustness and fairness transfer, data- and privacy-constrained settings, and reliably preserving rare or structured behavior.

papers_seen.author: Dominguez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable model-compression paradigm that transfers predictive behavior and internal representations from larger, high-capacity teacher models into smaller, more efficient student models. Across modalities and tasks, KD methods—ranging from softened-logit matching to intermediate-feature alignment, attention imitation, multi-teacher and online schemes, and data-side strategies—enable practical tradeoffs between accuracy and efficiency when deployed under latency, memory, or privacy constraints. Successful distillation depends on matching signals to student capacity, choosing or synthesizing appropriate data, and composing KD with complementary compression tools (pruning, quantization, compact-architecture pretraining). Remaining empirical and theoretical gaps include robustness under distribution shift, teacher–student mismatch, distillation with little or no real data, and principled selection of transfer objectives for constrained students.

papers_seen.author: Le
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has evolved into a central and versatile technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, efficient student models while maintaining competitive performance. By transferring knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to resource-constrained students, knowledge distillation addresses critical deployment challenges including latency reduction, memory efficiency, energy consumption, and privacy concerns. This synthesis examines the core mechanisms, practical applications, and challenges of knowledge distillation across vision, language, and specialized domains.

papers_seen.author: Hernandez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Practical Strategies, and Limits
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile framework for transferring knowledge from large teacher models to smaller student models to reduce inference cost, memory footprint, and latency while retaining much of the teacher’s performance. The literature frames KD as a family of techniques—logit/soft-target matching, intermediate-feature and attention imitation, multi-stage or multi-teacher schemes, data synthesis and data-free approaches, and online or ensemble-to-single transfer—that are frequently combined with complementary compression methods such as pruning and quantization. Empirical successes span computer vision and natural language tasks (including machine translation and non-autoregressive generation), but practical deployment requires attention to teacher–student capacity alignment, data availability (or synthesis), and task-specific failure modes such as degradation on low-frequency phenomena. Recent work develops mechanisms to enable distillation under constrained or private data regimes and to integrate low-precision numerics, while other studies document limits and design principles that guide reliable real-world compression pipelines.

papers_seen.author: Walters
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Synthesis of Methods, Applications, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large, high-performing neural networks into smaller, deployable models by transferring information from a teacher to a student. As a practical toolkit, distillation uses richer supervision than hard labels and can be combined with pruning, quantization, and architecture search to meet deployment constraints. It has been validated across computer vision, natural language processing, speech, recommendation, and federated settings, and is especially useful when latency, memory, or privacy concerns preclude using full-size models. Effective application requires careful design of what to transfer, how to align teacher and student capacities, and how to handle limited or private data.

papers_seen.author: Richardson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Multi-Strategy Framework for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and pragmatic approach for compressing large neural networks into smaller, deployable students. When treated as a multi-strategy engineering pipeline—combining soft-target supervision, intermediate-representation alignment, multi-teacher curricula, and complementary compression methods—KD enables substantial reductions in model size and latency while often preserving most of the teacher’s performance. However, KD is not a universal solution: its success depends on teacher quality, student capacity, data regimes, and careful design choices to avoid transferred errors or degraded rare-case behavior. Practitioners should therefore treat KD as a composable tool within broader compression and evaluation pipelines rather than as a single off-the-shelf recipe.

papers_seen.author: Garrison
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has become a core strategy for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students while retaining much of teacher performance. A broad family of KD mechanisms—soft-target matching, intermediate-feature imitation, layer-wise alignment, adversarial and contrastive objectives, and data-side strategies—supports diverse deployment constraints (latency, memory, privacy, heterogeneous hardware). In practice, KD is most effective when combined with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture-aware design) and when distillation choices (what to transfer, how to align teacher/student, and what data to use) are matched to the task and constraints. Remaining challenges include principled selection of distilled signals, robustness under domain shift and low-frequency phenomena, handling data-free or privacy-constrained settings, and automated student design for target hardware.

papers_seen.author: Chambers
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: An Essential and Versatile Framework for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and indispensable technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. By enabling the transfer of knowledge from computationally expensive teacher models to lightweight student networks, knowledge distillation addresses critical practical challenges in model deployment across diverse domains. This paper argues that knowledge distillation represents a core, composable component of modern compression pipelines that should be treated as an essential engineering paradigm rather than a simple algorithmic trick.

papers_seen.author: Lyons
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and versatile technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach transfers knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to resource-constrained student models, enabling deployment across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, speech recognition, and graph neural networks. The field encompasses multiple methodologies ranging from soft-target matching and feature-level imitation to multi-teacher pipelines and data-free approaches, addressing critical practical challenges in model deployment while presenting important limitations that require careful consideration.

papers_seen.author: Peck
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Applications, and Practical Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient student models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach enables the practical deployment of high-performing deep learning systems in resource-constrained environments by transferring knowledge from larger teacher models to compact students. The technique encompasses multiple methodologies including soft-target matching, feature-level mimicking, and intermediate representation alignment, while addressing practical challenges such as data scarcity, privacy constraints, and architecture heterogeneity across diverse domains including computer vision and natural language processing.

papers_seen.author: Sparks
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Practical Strategies, and Limits
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses high-capacity teacher models into smaller, deployable student models by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations. A broad toolkit has emerged—soft-target (logit) matching, intermediate-feature and attention-level mimicry, progressive and structural replacement, multi-teacher schedules, data-free and privacy-aware variants, and meta- or online-teaching strategies. In practice, distillation is routinely combined with pruning, quantization, and architecture-aware design to meet deployment constraints. Effectiveness depends on choosing appropriate transfer targets for the task and student capacity, handling limited or private data, and validating robustness under distribution shift. This synthesis summarizes current approaches, practical patterns for deployment, and common failure modes to guide applied use of distillation in NLP and related domains.

papers_seen.author: Fletcher
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Composable, but Context-Sensitive Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a widely adopted approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students by transferring information beyond hard labels. KD provides a flexible toolkit—matching logits, aligning features or intermediate layers, ensembling teachers, and integrating with pruning/quantization—that often yields strong accuracy/efficiency trade-offs for vision, NLP, and other domains. However, KD’s effectiveness depends on data availability, teacher-student capacity alignment, optimization dynamics, and the potential transfer of teacher biases; addressing these requires task-aware design, careful augmentation or data synthesis, and privacy-preserving or multi-teacher protocols when needed.

papers_seen.author: Webb
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Essential Techniques for Practical Deep Learning Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression have become fundamental techniques for enabling the deployment of large neural networks in resource-constrained environments. These methods transfer knowledge from computationally expensive teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models, addressing critical challenges in modern deep learning including inference latency, memory requirements, and computational costs. By combining diverse distillation strategies with complementary compression methods, practitioners can achieve substantial reductions in model size and inference cost while preserving competitive accuracy across vision, language, and specialized domains.

papers_seen.author: Lane
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a fundamental technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, deployable student models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach transfers knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to resource-constrained student networks, enabling practical deployment in latency-, memory-, and energy-limited environments across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, and multimodal systems. The technique encompasses multiple transfer mechanisms and methodologies, with success depending on careful design choices regarding what knowledge to transfer, teacher-student alignment, and integration with complementary compression techniques.

papers_seen.author: Burgess
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large, high-capacity teacher models into smaller, deployable student models by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations. The technique has expanded from matching softened output logits to include intermediate-feature mimicry, attention and relational objectives, multi-teacher and online schemes, and data- or privacy-aware variants. Practical success depends on careful choices about what to transfer, student capacity and architecture, data availability (including data-free methods), and how distillation is combined with complementary compression approaches such as pruning and quantization. Key open problems include robustness and fairness under distillation, handling distribution shift and low-frequency phenomena, principled student architecture design, and reliable evaluation for deployment.

papers_seen.author: Foster
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large teacher models into smaller student models by transferring predictive behavior and internal signals. Across deep learning and NLP, KD has evolved into a flexible, composable toolkit—encompassing softened-output matching, intermediate-feature and attention alignment, multi-teacher and online protocols, and data-free variants—that is routinely combined with pruning, quantization, and architecture design to meet deployment constraints. Practical success depends on teacher quality, teacher–student alignment, data availability, and targeted evaluation for robustness and rare-token behavior; when used with task-aware diagnostics and complementary compression methods, KD yields strong accuracy–efficiency trade-offs for resource-constrained deployment.

papers_seen.author: Allison
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and versatile approach for compressing large models into efficient students that retain much of the teacher’s performance. KD techniques—spanning logits-based soft-target transfer, intermediate feature alignment, and data-free synthesis—enable deployment of high-performing models on resource-constrained devices while also offering benefits in robustness and interpretability. When paired with task-aware design and careful teacher selection, distillation can produce compact models that meet real-world latency, memory, and privacy constraints without large sacrifices in accuracy.

papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Default, Task-Aware Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be treated as the primary tool for compressing large models into efficient students for deployment in deep learning and NLP. KD offers flexible mechanisms to transfer predictive behavior and internal representations from teachers to students, enabling substantial reductions in model size and latency while preserving much of the original performance. However, KD is not a one-size-fits-all recipe: its success depends on careful, task-aware design choices (e.g., which signals to transfer, teacher selection, data regimes, and complementary compression techniques) and on explicit strategies to detect and mitigate teacher error propagation. When applied thoughtfully and combined with other compression and deployment-aware methods, KD yields practical, high-fidelity compressed models across modalities and tasks.

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and indispensable technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, efficient models suitable for resource-constrained deployment. By enabling the transfer of knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to lightweight student networks, knowledge distillation addresses critical practical challenges in model deployment across diverse domains including computer vision and natural language processing. This framework encompasses multiple complementary mechanisms and should be treated as a central, composable component of modern compression pipelines rather than a standalone technique, providing significant reductions in model size, inference latency, and computational cost while preserving competitive predictive performance.

papers_seen.author: Jimenez
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP

In practice distillation is most effective when integrated with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and when design choices are aligned to student capacity, available data, and deployment constraints. Remaining limitations concern optimization gaps between teacher and student, transfer of undesirable teacher behaviors, robustness under distribution shift, and preserving rare‑case or low‑frequency phenomenon.

This approach has become fundamental across computer vision, natural language processing, and specialized domains, addressing the critical challenge of reducing computational overhead and memory requirements while maintaining competitive performance. The technique encompasses diverse strategies ranging from soft label guidance to intermediate layer alignment and operates through the transfer of learned knowledge from teacher to student networks.

This synthesis summarizes what is known about KD’s mechanisms, common variants, empirical strengths, and principal limitations, and it outlines recurring design principles for effective compression in deep learning and NLP.

However, distillation is not a universal remedy: its effectiveness depends on choices about what is transferred, available data, and how student and teacher internals align. Practical deployments benefit from treating KD as a multi-strategy engineering problem—selecting appropriate distillation targets, leveraging multi-teacher or data-free options when necessary, and addressing optimization gaps and low-frequency phenomena through task-aware interventions.

papers_seen.author: Huang
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a versatile and essential technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient student models while maintaining competitive performance. By transferring knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to resource-constrained students, this approach enables practical deployment across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, and machine translation. Knowledge distillation encompasses multiple complementary mechanisms and methodologies, addressing critical challenges in model size, inference latency, memory consumption, and computational efficiency in real-world deployment scenarios.

papers_seen.author: Zuniga
papers_seen.title: Large scale distributed neural network training through online distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Techniques such as ensembling and distillation promise model quality improvements when paired with almost any base model. However, due to increased test-time cost (for ensembles) and increased complexity of the training pipeline (for distillation), these techniques are challenging to use in industrial settings. In this paper we explore a variant of distillation which is relatively straightforward to use as it does not require a complicated multi-stage setup or many new hyperparameters. Our first claim is that online distillation enables us to use extra parallelism to fit very large datasets about twice as fast. Crucially, we can still speed up training even after we have already reached the point at which additional parallelism provides no benefit for synchronous or asynchronous stochastic gradient descent. Two neural networks trained on disjoint subsets of the data can share knowledge by encouraging each model to agree with the predictions the other model would have made. These predictions can come from a stale version of the other model so they can be safely computed using weights that only rarely get transmitted. Our second claim is that online distillation is a cost-effective way to make the exact predictions of a model dramatically more reproducible. We support our claims using experiments on the Criteo Display Ad Challenge dataset, ImageNet, and the largest to-date dataset used for neural language modeling, containing $6\times 10^{11}$ tokens and based on the Common Crawl repository of web data.

papers_seen.author: Morales
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: What Is Known About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a mature, widely adopted approach for producing compact student models that retain much of the performance of larger teacher networks. Across vision, language, multimodal, and retrieval tasks, KD methods transfer knowledge via soft logits, intermediate representations, attention or feature matching, and related objectives; they are often combined with pruning, quantization, or architecture search to meet deployment constraints. Empirical work shows KD can yield substantial reductions in model size and latency with modest performance loss, but success depends on careful teacher–student design, data availability, and task-aware choices. Open directions include principled student architecture selection, robust transfer of rare or structural behaviors, privacy- and data-free pipelines, and preserving robustness and fairness during compression.

papers_seen.author: Maddox
papers_seen.title: BERT-EMD: Many-to-Many Layer Mapping for BERT Compression with Earth Mover's Distance
papers_seen.abstract: Pre-trained language models (e.g., BERT) have achieved significant success in various natural language processing (NLP) tasks. However, high storage and computational costs obstruct pre-trained language models to be effectively deployed on resource-constrained devices. In this paper, we propose a novel BERT distillation method based on many-to-many layer mapping, which allows each intermediate student layer to learn from any intermediate teacher layers. In this way, our model can learn from different teacher layers adaptively for various NLP tasks. %motivated by the intuition that different NLP tasks require different levels of linguistic knowledge contained in the intermediate layers of BERT. In addition, we leverage Earth Mover's Distance (EMD) to compute the minimum cumulative cost that must be paid to transform knowledge from teacher network to student network. EMD enables the effective matching for many-to-many layer mapping. %EMD can be applied to network layers with different sizes and effectively measures semantic distance between the teacher network and student network. Furthermore, we propose a cost attention mechanism to learn the layer weights used in EMD automatically, which is supposed to further improve the model's performance and accelerate convergence time. Extensive experiments on GLUE benchmark demonstrate that our model achieves competitive performance compared to strong competitors in terms of both accuracy and model compression.

papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Applications, and Practical Strategies
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a fundamental technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient student models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach transfers knowledge from complex teacher models to resource-constrained students, enabling practical deployment of state-of-the-art systems across computer vision, natural language processing, and specialized domains. By addressing critical constraints of latency, memory efficiency, and computational cost, knowledge distillation has become essential for making sophisticated deep learning models practical for real-world applications.

papers_seen.author: Roberts
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses high-capacity teacher networks into smaller student models by transferring useful information beyond hard labels. In practice, distillation uses a variety of signals (soft logits, intermediate features, attention maps, or relational/structural information) and is combined with other compression methods to meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Its empirical success across vision, language, and multimodal tasks has made it a core component of production compression pipelines, but success depends on careful teacher–student matching, data strategies, and explicit handling of robustness and rare or safety-critical behaviors.

papers_seen.author: Schultz
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Methods, Applications, and Practical Constraints
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a family of techniques for transferring knowledge from larger teacher models into smaller student models to reduce model size, latency, and resource use while preserving task performance. Distillation mechanisms include transferring softened output distributions, matching intermediate representations, ensembling or online teacher strategies, and data- or task-aware adaptations. KD has been applied across domains — from recommendation and ranking to object detection, non-autoregressive machine translation, and federated settings — and is often combined with complementary compression methods. Its effectiveness depends on teacher quality, the choice of distilled targets, student capacity, and the match between training data and deployment conditions; these dependencies motivate pragmatic design choices and ongoing research into robust, data-efficient, and privacy-aware distillation pipelines.

papers_seen.author: Cole
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: An Essential, Task-Aware Strategy for Practical Deep Learning Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a fundamental technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, deployable student models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach transfers knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to resource-constrained students through diverse mechanisms, enabling efficient inference across domains including computer vision and natural language processing. However, effective distillation is not automatic—it requires careful consideration of what knowledge to transfer, how to align teacher and student architectures, and how to handle data constraints. This paper argues that knowledge distillation represents an indispensable yet context-dependent tool for modern deep learning deployment, requiring principled design choices and integration with complementary compression techniques.

papers_seen.author: Atkins
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical family of techniques for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students by transferring predictive behavior, intermediate representations, or synthesized training signals. KD methods range from matching softened teacher outputs to aligning internal features, and can be combined with pruning, quantization, or architecture search to meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Empirical work shows KD often yields strong size–performance tradeoffs across vision and language tasks, but success depends on careful teacher–student design, data availability, and task-aware objectives; important open problems remain in data-free transfer, robust transfer under distribution shift, and avoiding propagation of teacher artifacts.

However, distillation is not a universal remedy: its effectiveness depends on choices about what is transferred, available data, and how student and teacher internals align. Practical deployments benefit from treating KD as a multi-strategy engineering problem—selecting appropriate distillation targets, leveraging multi-teacher or data-free options when necessary, and addressing optimization gaps and low-frequency phenomena through task-aware interventions.

papers_seen.author: Knight
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large, high-capacity teacher models into smaller, deployable student models by transferring predictive behavior and representational signals. The technique encompasses soft-target matching, feature- and layer-level mimicry, attention transfer, multi-teacher and ensemble-to-single strategies, and data-aware or data-free variants. When combined deliberately with complementary methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and adapted to task- and data-constraints, distillation yields practical trade-offs between efficiency and accuracy and enables deployment under latency, memory, energy, and privacy constraints. Practical success depends on teacher–student alignment, careful selection of distilled signals, and evaluation for robustness, distribution shift, and failure modes.

papers_seen.author: Murphy
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Practical and Essential Framework for Neural Network Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models suitable for deployment in resource-constrained environments. This approach transfers knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to lightweight student models through multiple complementary mechanisms, enabling practical deployment across diverse domains while maintaining competitive performance. The technique addresses critical real-world deployment constraints including model size, inference latency, memory requirements, and computational costs, making it essential for bringing state-of-the-art deep learning systems to practical applications.

papers_seen.author: Harvey
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: A Targeted Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses larger teacher models into smaller student models by transferring predictive behavior or internal representations. Across vision and NLP, KD supports latency- and memory-constrained deployment by combining soft-target matching, feature-level alignment, online and ensemble strategies, and data- or privacy-aware variants. Practical pipelines increasingly blend multiple techniques (representation distillation, architecture-aware mappings, data synthesis, and training-time teacher adaptation) to balance accuracy, efficiency, and deployment constraints. Open challenges remain in teacher–student mismatch, data unavailability, distribution shift, and fairness/privacy trade-offs.

papers_seen.author: Gardner
papers_seen.title: Adversarially Robust Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is effective for producing small, high-performance neural networks for classification, but these small networks are vulnerable to adversarial attacks. This paper studies how adversarial robustness transfers from teacher to student during knowledge distillation. We find that a large amount of robustness may be inherited by the student even when distilled on only clean images. Second, we introduce Adversarially Robust Distillation (ARD) for distilling robustness onto student networks. In addition to producing small models with high test accuracy like conventional distillation, ARD also passes the superior robustness of large networks onto the student. In our experiments, we find that ARD student models decisively outperform adversarially trained networks of identical architecture in terms of robust accuracy, surpassing state-of-the-art methods on standard robustness benchmarks. Finally, we adapt recent fast adversarial training methods to ARD for accelerated robust distillation.

papers_seen.author: Castaneda
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Deep Learning and NLP: Powerful, Practical, but Context-Dependent
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile technique for compressing large neural networks into efficient student models by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from teacher models. KD enables deployment of strong models under latency, memory, and compute constraints across vision, speech, and natural language tasks. However, the empirical success of distillation depends on careful choices about what to transfer, the availability and nature of data, teacher-student capacity alignment, and task-specific constraints. When combined with complementary compression methods and appropriate training curricula, KD routinely yields compact models that retain much of teacher performance; conversely, poorly designed distillation can propagate teacher biases or fail to capture rare phenomena. This paper argues that KD should be treated as a core tool in model-compression toolboxes while emphasizing principled, task-aware design and evaluation.

papers_seen.author: Mata
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Applications, and Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and versatile technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient student models while maintaining competitive performance. By transferring knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to resource-constrained student networks, this approach enables practical deployment of state-of-the-art deep learning systems across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, machine translation, speech recognition, and specialized applications. Knowledge distillation encompasses multiple methodologies and addresses critical deployment challenges such as reducing computational cost, memory consumption, and inference latency, though optimal success requires careful design of teacher-student alignment and task-specific adaptation.

papers_seen.author: Hughes
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) transfers predictive behavior and internal representations from larger teacher models to smaller student models to reduce inference cost and memory while often preserving accuracy. Across domains, KD has evolved from matching softened outputs to a broad family of methods that include intermediate-feature and relational transfer, architecture-aware compression, data-free or synthetic-data procedures, and task-adaptive search. Empirical work shows substantial runtime and size reductions are achievable, but practical success depends on teacher–student alignment, data availability, and integration with complementary techniques such as pruning, quantization, or architecture search. Open challenges include robustness under distribution shift, reliably transferring structural or low-frequency knowledge, and designing student-aware teachers and training curricula.

papers_seen.author: Lester
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a core model-compression approach that trains compact student models to reproduce the behavior of larger teacher models, enabling deployment in resource- and latency-constrained settings. The literature identifies multiple mechanisms (soft-target matching, intermediate-feature alignment, attention transfer, and progressive module replacement), practical pipelines (pretraining compact architectures, domain adaptation before distillation, and multi-source supervision), and common integrations with pruning, quantization, and architecture search. Empirical work shows KD can preserve much of a teacher’s performance across vision, speech, and language tasks, but realizing these gains in production requires careful attention to teacher–student capacity alignment, data availability (or synthesis), domain shift, and robustness to rare phenomena.

papers_seen.author: Le
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has evolved into a central and versatile technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, efficient student models while maintaining competitive performance. By transferring knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to resource-constrained students, knowledge distillation addresses critical deployment challenges including latency reduction, memory efficiency, energy consumption, and privacy concerns. This synthesis examines the core mechanisms, practical applications, and challenges of knowledge distillation across vision, language, and specialized domains.

papers_seen.author: Durham
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as an Essential and Task-Aware Strategy for Practical Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models suitable for deployment in resource-constrained environments. By transferring knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to compact student networks, knowledge distillation enables significant reductions in model size, memory requirements, and inference latency while maintaining competitive performance. However, successful knowledge distillation requires careful attention to task-specific design choices, teacher-student alignment, and complementary compression techniques rather than serving as a universal one-size-fits-all solution.

papers_seen.author: Tran
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as an Essential but Context‑Sensitive Toolkit for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, high‑impact approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students while retaining much of teacher performance. KD succeeds by transferring softened outputs, intermediate representations, or relational signals, but its reliability and efficiency depend on careful alignment of objectives, data, and student capacity. I argue that KD should be treated as a central component of compression pipelines that is intentionally combined with complementary methods and rigorous evaluation rather than as a one‑size‑fits‑all solution.

papers_seen.author: Brown
papers_seen.title: Unified Visual Transformer Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Vision transformers (ViTs) have gained popularity recently. Even without customized image operators such as convolutions, ViTs can yield competitive performance when properly trained on massive data. However, the computational overhead of ViTs remains prohibitive, due to stacking multi-head self-attention modules and else. Compared to the vast literature and prevailing success in compressing convolutional neural networks, the study of Vision Transformer compression has also just emerged, and existing works focused on one or two aspects of compression. This paper proposes a unified ViT compression framework that seamlessly assembles three effective techniques: pruning, layer skipping, and knowledge distillation. We formulate a budget-constrained, end-to-end optimization framework, targeting jointly learning model weights, layer-wise pruning ratios/masks, and skip configurations, under a distillation loss. The optimization problem is then solved using the primal-dual algorithm. Experiments are conducted with several ViT variants, e.g. DeiT and T2T-ViT backbones on the ImageNet dataset, and our approach consistently outperforms recent competitors. For example, DeiT-Tiny can be trimmed down to 50\% of the original FLOPs almost without losing accuracy. Codes are available online:~\url{https://github.com/VITA-Group/UVC}.

papers_seen.author: Chapman
papers_seen.title: What is Known About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly adopted family of techniques for compressing large teacher models into smaller, efficient student models by transferring predictive behavior, intermediate representations, or synthesized training signals. KD is applied across modalities and tasks to reduce model size, latency, and energy while retaining much of the original performance. Successful application of KD typically treats it as a composable component of a broader compression pipeline (together with pruning, quantization, and architecture search), adapts the choice of distilled signal to task and data constraints, and evaluates students under realistic distribution shift and deployment requirements. Important open issues include preserving robustness, fairness and rare-behavior transfer, operating without original training data, and principled teacher–student architecture alignment.

papers_seen.author: Caldwell
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large, high-capacity models into smaller, faster models by transferring behavior or representations from a teacher to a student. It is widely used to enable deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints across modalities (vision, language, speech, multimodal) and tasks (classification, retrieval, generation, segmentation). Effective distillation combines multiple signals (soft targets, intermediate-feature matching, layer-wise supervision, adversarial training, and ensemble guidance) and is commonly paired with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search). Practical pipelines must balance teacher selection, data regimes, and student capacity to approach teacher performance while meeting resource constraints.

papers_seen.author: Mejia
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, widely adopted family of techniques for transferring behavior from large teacher models to smaller student models to meet deployment constraints in deep learning and NLP. KD methods reduce model size, inference latency, and memory cost while often preserving much of teacher performance. However, KD is not a universal panacea: its success depends on careful teacher–student alignment, choice of distilled signals, data strategies, and integration with complementary compression primitives. When applied as a configurable component of a compression pipeline, KD delivers strong accuracy/efficiency trade-offs while posing open challenges around robustness, fairness, and data- or privacy-constrained scenarios.

papers_seen.author: Ramos
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression have become essential techniques for deploying large neural networks in resource-constrained environments. These methods enable the transfer of knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models, significantly reducing computational requirements, inference latency, and memory consumption while maintaining competitive performance. Applications span diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, graph neural networks, and multimodal learning, with approaches ranging from output-level soft-target matching to feature-level and attention-based transfers. Practical success depends on careful design of distillation objectives, teacher-student alignment, and integration with complementary compression techniques.

papers_seen.author: Leblanc
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Default for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a fundamental and versatile technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, deployable student models while preserving competitive performance. This paper argues that KD should serve as the default starting point within model compression pipelines because it provides a flexible, widely applicable framework for transferring behavior from high-capacity teachers to resource-constrained students across diverse domains. When strategically combined with complementary compression techniques and guided by careful design choices, knowledge distillation enables practical deployment of state-of-the-art deep learning systems while meeting critical real-world constraints on latency, memory consumption, and computational efficiency.

papers_seen.author: Sheppard
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a fundamental technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient student models while maintaining competitive performance. By transferring knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to resource-constrained students, knowledge distillation enables efficient deployment across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, machine translation, and speech recognition. The approach has evolved from simple soft-label matching to a comprehensive toolkit encompassing intermediate representation transfer, feature-level distillation, multi-teacher ensemble strategies, and self-supervised methods. While knowledge distillation frequently yields substantial gains in model size, latency, and memory with modest performance loss, its effectiveness depends on critical factors including teacher quality, student capacity, data characteristics, and the specific form of knowledge transferred.

papers_seen.author: Bray
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Applications, and Practical Considerations
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and versatile technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient student models suitable for deployment in resource-constrained environments. This approach transfers knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to compact student networks, enabling significant reductions in model size, memory requirements, and inference latency while maintaining competitive performance. Knowledge distillation encompasses multiple methodologies operating at different levels and has proven effective across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, machine translation, and multimodal learning. Practical success requires careful consideration of distillation targets, teacher-student alignment, data availability, and integration with complementary compression techniques.

papers_seen.author: Griffith
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: A Practical Framework for Efficient Deep Learning and NLP Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and versatile approach for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while preserving competitive performance. By transferring knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to resource-constrained student networks, knowledge distillation enables practical deployment of state-of-the-art deep learning systems across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and speech recognition. This framework encompasses multiple distillation mechanisms, complementary compression techniques, and practical design considerations that collectively address critical deployment challenges including reduced latency, memory footprint, and computational cost.

papers_seen.author: Taylor
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: State of the Art and Practical Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a widely-adopted approach for compressing large neural networks into smaller, deployable student models by transferring knowledge from high-capacity teacher models. This technique addresses critical challenges in deploying sophisticated deep learning systems on resource-constrained devices while maintaining competitive performance. Knowledge distillation encompasses diverse methodologies including soft-target matching, intermediate representation alignment, and data-aware approaches, and can be effectively combined with complementary compression techniques such as pruning, quantization, and architecture search. Practical success depends on careful design choices regarding teacher-student capacity matching, selection of appropriate distillation objectives, and alignment with specific deployment constraints including latency, memory, privacy, and computational efficiency.

papers_seen.author: Wood
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a model compression technique that transfers knowledge from a larger teacher model to a smaller student model, enabling efficient deployment of neural networks while maintaining competitive performance. This technique has become increasingly important across various domains including computer vision, natural language processing, and specialized applications. The approach addresses the critical challenge of deploying complex, high-performing deep learning models on resource-constrained devices by enabling smaller models to achieve comparable results to their larger counterparts.

papers_seen.author: Lewis
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a model compression technique that enables the transfer of knowledge from large, complex neural networks (teacher models) to smaller, more efficient student models. This approach has become increasingly important for deploying state-of-the-art deep learning and NLP models in resource-constrained environments, particularly on edge devices and mobile platforms. By training student networks to mimic teacher outputs, knowledge distillation addresses the fundamental challenge of maintaining competitive performance while significantly reducing model size, computational cost, and inference latency. The technique has been successfully applied across diverse domains including machine translation, information retrieval, visual recognition, and graph neural networks.

papers_seen.author: Hernandez
papers_seen.title: R2L: Distilling Neural Radiance Field to Neural Light Field for Efficient Novel View Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Recent research explosion on Neural Radiance Field (NeRF) shows the encouraging potential to represent complex scenes with neural networks. One major drawback of NeRF is its prohibitive inference time: Rendering a single pixel requires querying the NeRF network hundreds of times. To resolve it, existing efforts mainly attempt to reduce the number of required sampled points. However, the problem of iterative sampling still exists. On the other hand, Neural Light Field (NeLF) presents a more straightforward representation over NeRF in novel view synthesis -- the rendering of a pixel amounts to one single forward pass without ray-marching. In this work, we present a deep residual MLP network (88 layers) to effectively learn the light field. We show the key to successfully learning such a deep NeLF network is to have sufficient data, for which we transfer the knowledge from a pre-trained NeRF model via data distillation. Extensive experiments on both synthetic and real-world scenes show the merits of our method over other counterpart algorithms. On the synthetic scenes, we achieve 26-35x FLOPs reduction (per camera ray) and 28-31x runtime speedup, meanwhile delivering significantly better (1.4-2.8 dB average PSNR improvement) rendering quality than NeRF without any customized parallelism requirement.
