papers_seen.author: Contreras
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a core approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students across vision, language, and multimodal settings. KD encompasses matching teacher soft targets, aligning intermediate representations, transferring relational or attention patterns, and operating in data-limited, privacy-sensitive, or federated scenarios. When combined with complementary techniques such as pruning, quantization, architecture search, and careful pre-training, KD enables production-ready trade-offs between accuracy, latency, and memory. However, practical deployment requires attention to teacher quality, student capacity and architecture, data availability, and robustness to distribution shift and low-frequency phenomena.

papers_seen.author: Liu
papers_seen.title: Enabling Multimodal Generation on CLIP via Vision-Language Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: The recent large-scale vision-language pre-training (VLP) of dual-stream architectures (e.g., CLIP) with a tremendous amount of image-text pair data, has shown its superiority on various multimodal alignment tasks. Despite its success, the resulting models are not capable of multimodal generative tasks due to the weak text encoder. To tackle this problem, we propose to augment the dual-stream VLP model with a textual pre-trained language model (PLM) via vision-language knowledge distillation (VLKD), enabling the capability for multimodal generation. VLKD is pretty data- and computation-efficient compared to the pre-training from scratch. Experimental results show that the resulting model has strong zero-shot performance on multimodal generation tasks, such as open-ended visual question answering and image captioning. For example, it achieves 44.5% zero-shot accuracy on the VQAv2 dataset, surpassing the previous state-of-the-art zero-shot model with $7\times$ fewer parameters. Furthermore, the original textual language understanding and generation ability of the PLM is maintained after VLKD, which makes our model versatile for both multimodal and unimodal tasks.

papers_seen.author: Graham
papers_seen.title: What Is Known About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broad, practical framework for compressing large teacher models into smaller student models by transferring predictive behavior, internal representations, or synthesized training signals. Across vision and language domains, KD enables large reductions in model size and inference cost while often preserving much of the teacher's performance. Empirical practice treats KD as a composable element combined with pruning, quantization, architecture search, curricula, and data-synthesis strategies. Key practical considerations include choosing what to transfer (logits, intermediate features, attention), aligning teacher signals to student capacity, and handling limited or private data. Important open problems remain in robustness, fairness transfer, principled target selection, and automating task-adaptive compression pipelines.

papers_seen.author: Everett
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Cornerstone Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and widely-adopted technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, efficient models while preserving competitive performance. By transferring knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to resource-constrained student networks, knowledge distillation enables practical deployment of sophisticated deep learning systems across diverse applications including computer vision, natural language processing, and machine translation. The technique encompasses multiple complementary mechanisms including soft-target matching, intermediate representation alignment, and multi-teacher frameworks, and is most effective when combined with careful design choices and complementary compression strategies.

papers_seen.author: Andrews
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: A Versatile Yet Context-Dependent Strategy for Efficient Deep Learning Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a fundamental technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient student models while preserving predictive performance. This approach transfers knowledge from teacher models to students through various mechanisms, enabling deployment in resource-constrained environments across vision, language, and multimodal domains. However, the effectiveness of knowledge distillation depends critically on contextual design choices including what knowledge is transferred, teacher-student capacity alignment, data availability, and task-specific constraints, making it a powerful but not universally sufficient compression tool.

papers_seen.author: Conley
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: A Practical Necessity for Efficient Deep Learning and NLP Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a foundational and practical technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, deployable student models. By transferring knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to resource-constrained students, knowledge distillation enables substantial reductions in model size, inference latency, and computational requirements while maintaining competitive performance. This approach encompasses diverse mechanisms—from soft-target matching and feature alignment to data-free methods—and achieves maximum effectiveness when integrated with complementary compression strategies. While knowledge distillation addresses critical deployment challenges across computer vision, natural language processing, and specialized domains, its success fundamentally depends on careful design choices regarding teacher-student capacity alignment, selection of what knowledge to transfer, data availability, and task-specific adaptation.

papers_seen.author: Weeks
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as Essential Framework for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and versatile technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, deployable models while preserving competitive performance. By transferring knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to constrained student networks, this approach enables substantial reductions in computational requirements, model size, and inference latency. Knowledge distillation encompasses multiple complementary strategies including soft-label matching, intermediate representation transfer, and data-free variants, making it essential for practical deployment across diverse domains. However, effective distillation requires careful attention to task-specific constraints, teacher-student alignment, data availability, and integration with complementary compression techniques.

papers_seen.author: Terry
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: An Essential, Practical Core for Compression — with Limits and Design Requirements
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central technique for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. KD enables efficient deployment under latency, memory, and compute constraints by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from teacher to student. While KD is broadly effective across modalities and tasks, realizing reliable production gains requires combining KD with task-aware design, complementary compression methods, and careful handling of data, teacher–student alignment, and robustness concerns.

papers_seen.author: Gibbs
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: What We Know About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-capacity teacher models into smaller student models by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations. Over the past decade KD has grown from simple soft-target matching into a diverse toolkit that includes feature- and layer-level mimicry, multi-teacher and staged procedures, data- and privacy-aware variants, and combinations with pruning, quantization, and architecture search. Empirical work demonstrates that KD can yield substantial efficiency gains while retaining much of teacher performance, but outcomes depend on careful choices about distilled signals, teacher–student alignment, data availability, and complementary compression strategies.

papers_seen.author: Shaw
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Fundamental and Composable Strategy for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a central technique for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable student networks while maintaining competitive performance. By transferring knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to resource-constrained students, distillation enables significant reductions in model size, memory, latency, and computational cost across diverse domains including computer vision and natural language processing. This review argues that knowledge distillation should be treated as a foundational and composable tool in modern model compression pipelines, though its practical success depends critically on careful design choices, teacher-student alignment, data strategies, and integration with complementary compression methods.

papers_seen.author: Gutierrez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a flexible and practical framework for compressing large neural networks into smaller, deployable student models while preserving much of the teacher's performance. The technique transfers knowledge through multiple mechanisms including soft-target matching, intermediate representation alignment, and relational objectives, enabling substantial reductions in model size, latency, and memory requirements. Knowledge distillation has proven effective across diverse domains including natural language processing and computer vision, and when combined with complementary compression techniques, provides a versatile solution for deploying sophisticated deep learning systems in resource-constrained environments.

papers_seen.author: Moore
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Default for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) offers a compact, flexible framework to transfer behavior and internal structure from large teacher models to smaller students, enabling deployment under latency, memory, and compute constraints. KD succeeds across modalities when combined with data strategies and complementary compression (pruning, quantization, architecture design), but its practical use requires careful teacher–student capacity alignment, attention to data availability and privacy, and explicit evaluation for robustness and rare or safety-critical behaviors. With principled design and complementary techniques, KD should be treated as the default starting point for model compression pipelines, while ongoing work addresses data-free distillation, federated and heterogeneous-device settings, and scalable/online protocols.

papers_seen.author: Lane
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a fundamental technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, deployable student models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach transfers knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to resource-constrained student networks, enabling practical deployment in latency-, memory-, and energy-limited environments across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, and multimodal systems. The technique encompasses multiple transfer mechanisms and methodologies, with success depending on careful design choices regarding what knowledge to transfer, teacher-student alignment, and integration with complementary compression techniques.

papers_seen.author: Romero
papers_seen.title: What We Know About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a widely adopted approach to compressing large neural networks into smaller, efficient students by transferring information from one or more teacher models. Over the last decade the field has matured from simple soft-target matching to a broad toolkit that includes intermediate-representation matching, attention- and layer-level objectives, multi-teacher and online schemes, data-free distillation, and combinations with pruning, quantization, and architecture search. Empirical evidence shows KD routinely produces substantial reductions in model size and latency while preserving much of the teacher’s performance when design choices—what to transfer, how to construct training data, and how to align teacher and student capacity—are carefully made. Remaining limits include sensitivity to data distribution shifts, propagation of teacher biases or errors, dependence on teacher quality and student capacity, and the need for automated, task-adaptive pipelines that balance efficiency with downstream objectives.

papers_seen.author: Gregory
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Foundational and Composable Framework for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation represents a fundamental and versatile technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, efficient student models suitable for resource-constrained deployment. By transferring knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to compact student networks through diverse mechanisms, distillation enables substantial reductions in computational cost, memory footprint, and inference latency while preserving competitive performance. This paper argues that knowledge distillation should be treated as a central, composable toolkit for model compression—not as a single recipe, but as a flexible framework that, when combined with complementary techniques and guided by careful design choices, enables practical deployment of state-of-the-art deep learning systems across computer vision, natural language processing, and specialized domains.

papers_seen.author: Doyle
papers_seen.title: DE-RRD: A Knowledge Distillation Framework for Recommender System
papers_seen.abstract: Recent recommender systems have started to employ knowledge distillation, which is a model compression technique distilling knowledge from a cumbersome model (teacher) to a compact model (student), to reduce inference latency while maintaining performance. The state-of-the-art methods have only focused on making the student model accurately imitate the predictions of the teacher model. They have a limitation in that the prediction results incompletely reveal the teacher's knowledge. In this paper, we propose a novel knowledge distillation framework for recommender system, called DE-RRD, which enables the student model to learn from the latent knowledge encoded in the teacher model as well as from the teacher's predictions. Concretely, DE-RRD consists of two methods: 1) Distillation Experts (DE) that directly transfers the latent knowledge from the teacher model. DE exploits "experts" and a novel expert selection strategy for effectively distilling the vast teacher's knowledge to the student with limited capacity. 2) Relaxed Ranking Distillation (RRD) that transfers the knowledge revealed from the teacher's prediction with consideration of the relaxed ranking orders among items. Our extensive experiments show that DE-RRD outperforms the state-of-the-art competitors and achieves comparable or even better performance to that of the teacher model with faster inference time.

papers_seen.author: Evans
papers_seen.title: Learning Compact Metrics for MT
papers_seen.abstract: Recent developments in machine translation and multilingual text generation have led researchers to adopt trained metrics such as COMET or BLEURT, which treat evaluation as a regression problem and use representations from multilingual pre-trained models such as XLM-RoBERTa or mBERT. Yet studies on related tasks suggest that these models are most efficient when they are large, which is costly and impractical for evaluation. We investigate the trade-off between multilinguality and model capacity with RemBERT, a state-of-the-art multilingual language model, using data from the WMT Metrics Shared Task. We present a series of experiments which show that model size is indeed a bottleneck for cross-lingual transfer, then demonstrate how distillation can help addressing this bottleneck, by leveraging synthetic data generation and transferring knowledge from one teacher to multiple students trained on related languages. Our method yields up to 10.5% improvement over vanilla fine-tuning and reaches 92.6% of RemBERT's performance using only a third of its parameters.

papers_seen.author: Lyons
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: A Practical Imperative for Deep Learning and NLP Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a fundamental and versatile technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, efficient student models while preserving competitive performance. By transferring knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to resource-constrained students, KD enables practical deployment of state-of-the-art deep learning and NLP systems across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, and machine translation. The technique encompasses multiple complementary methodologies spanning soft-target matching, intermediate representation transfer, multi-teacher fusion, and data-free synthesis. While KD has proven highly effective when carefully designed and integrated with complementary compression techniques, its success is not universal and depends critically on task requirements, teacher quality, data availability, student capacity, and alignment between deployment constraints and training design choices.

papers_seen.author: Dalton
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Applications, and Design Principles
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a fundamental and versatile technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient student models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach transfers knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to resource-constrained students through multiple complementary mechanisms including soft-label matching, feature-level supervision, and intermediate representation alignment. KD enables substantial reductions in computational requirements, memory footprint, and inference latency across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, machine translation, and multimodal learning, addressing critical real-world deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Peterson
papers_seen.title: The Central Role of Knowledge Distillation in Efficient and Robust NLP Models
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a unifying approach for producing smaller, faster, and often more robust models for NLP and deep learning broadly. When combined with architecture search, layer-wise matching, data-centric techniques, and privacy-aware protocols, distillation enables task-adaptive compression, domain adaptation, and practical deployment under latency, memory, and regulatory constraints. However, the benefits of distillation depend on how knowledge is represented, which data and augmentations are used during transfer, and whether the distillation procedure is aligned with downstream tasks; careful method design—rather than blind teacher-student pairing—is therefore required to realize its full promise.

papers_seen.author: Mueller
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Effective Strategies for Deploying Deep Learning Models in Resource-Constrained Environments
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful and practical technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach transfers knowledge from larger teacher models to smaller student models, enabling deployment in resource-constrained environments such as mobile devices and edge computing systems. By leveraging various distillation methodologies—from soft target matching to feature-level alignment—this technique addresses fundamental challenges in deep learning deployment without sacrificing model capability. Knowledge distillation has proven effective across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, and graph neural networks, making it a foundational technique in modern machine learning.

papers_seen.author: Thornton
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Default, Composable Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, versatile approach for producing compact models that retain much of the predictive capacity of larger teachers. When applied as a deliberate, task-aware element within a broader compression pipeline (including pretraining, pruning, and quantization), KD enables deployment under real-world latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Its many instantiations—soft-target matching, intermediate-feature alignment, attention- or layer-aware mappings, and multi-teacher or data-centric variants—make KD the recommended default starting point for model compression, provided designers attend to teacher quality, teacher–student capacity alignment, and dataset/regime-specific caveats.

papers_seen.author: Cisneros
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as an Essential, Context‑Aware Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and practically essential approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. When treated as a composable toolkit—incorporating soft-target matching, intermediate representation alignment, attention transfer, and data-side strategies—KD enables substantial reductions in model size, inference latency, and memory while often preserving much of teacher performance. Its success depends on deliberate teacher–student design, alignment of capacity and objectives, and integration with complementary techniques such as pruning, quantization, and architecture search; therefore KD should be applied as a context‑aware core of compression pipelines rather than as a one‑size‑fits‑all recipe.

papers_seen.author: Williams
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: A Practical and Essential Strategy for Deploying Deep Learning Systems
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression have emerged as fundamental techniques for enabling the deployment of large, computationally expensive neural networks in resource-constrained environments. These methods transfer knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models, achieving substantial reductions in parameter count, memory consumption, and inference latency while preserving competitive performance. The field encompasses diverse approaches ranging from output-level supervision to sophisticated multi-level knowledge transfer strategies, with successful applications across computer vision, natural language processing, machine translation, and specialized domains. While knowledge distillation offers significant practical benefits for real-world deployment, its effectiveness depends critically on careful design choices, proper alignment of teacher and student architectures, and thoughtful integration with complementary compression techniques.

papers_seen.author: Bruce
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Essential Strategies for Practical Deep Learning Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and versatile technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models suitable for deployment in resource-constrained environments. By transferring knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to lightweight student networks, knowledge distillation enables substantial reductions in model size, inference latency, and computational requirements while preserving competitive performance. This approach encompasses multiple complementary mechanisms and can be strategically combined with other compression techniques to address critical challenges in practical deployment across diverse applications in both computer vision and natural language processing.

papers_seen.author: Bell
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: An Essential Strategy for Practical Deep Learning and NLP Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and versatile technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. By transferring knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to lightweight student models, this approach addresses the critical challenge of deploying sophisticated deep learning systems in resource-constrained environments. The technique encompasses diverse methodologies including soft-target matching, feature-level mimicry, layer-wise alignment, and data-free approaches, with applications spanning natural language processing, computer vision, and specialized domains. This position argues that knowledge distillation represents not merely a complementary technique but a central and essential strategy that enables practical deployment across diverse applications and domains.

papers_seen.author: Reyes
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Core Techniques and Practical Implementation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and versatile technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient student models while maintaining competitive performance. By transferring knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to resource-constrained students, this approach enables practical deployment of state-of-the-art systems across diverse domains including computer vision and natural language processing. Knowledge distillation addresses critical real-world challenges such as computational efficiency, inference latency, memory constraints, and privacy preservation, making it an essential strategy for deploying sophisticated neural networks in resource-limited environments.

papers_seen.author: Benson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Comprehensive Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and versatile approach for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient student models while preserving competitive performance. This technique transfers knowledge from computationally expensive teacher models to resource-constrained students through various mechanisms, enabling practical deployment across diverse domains. Knowledge distillation addresses critical challenges in modern machine learning including reducing inference latency, memory requirements, computational costs, and enabling deployment on edge devices, while maintaining or approaching the performance of large teacher models across computer vision, natural language processing, speech recognition, and specialized domains.

papers_seen.author: Turner
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Task-Aware Default for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible means of producing compact student models that retain much of the performance of larger teachers. KD is not a single algorithm but a configurable toolkit—logit/soft-target matching, intermediate-feature and attention mimicry, multi-teacher and online schemes, and data-aware or data-free procedures—that, when matched to task constraints and combined with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search), reliably improves deployability in latency-, memory-, energy- and privacy-constrained environments. However, realizing KD’s benefits in production requires deliberate teacher–student design, careful data strategies (including handling limited or private data), attention to robustness and transferred failure modes, and empirical validation under deployment distributions. I argue KD should be the default starting point in compression pipelines, applied in a task-aware and composable way rather than as a one-size-fits-all cure.

papers_seen.author: Payne
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central but Contextual Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a mature, versatile approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students by transferring information beyond hard labels. KD enables substantial reductions in model size and inference cost while retaining much of teacher performance across vision, language, and multimodal tasks. However, KD is not universally sufficient: its success depends on data availability, teacher–student capacity alignment, optimization curricula, and deployment constraints (e.g., privacy, federated settings, and domain shift). Practical compression pipelines therefore treat KD as a core component to be combined with complementary strategies—multi-teacher schedules, selective sample distillation, domain-aware adaptation, architecture-aware design, and communication-efficient protocols—to produce reliable, production-ready compact models.

papers_seen.author: Berger
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation trains smaller ‘‘student’’ models to reproduce the behavior of larger ‘‘teacher’’ models, enabling dramatic reductions in parameters, latency, and memory while preserving much of task performance. Methods vary in what is transferred (soft logits, intermediate features, attention maps, or structural/relational signals), how teacher and student architectures are aligned, and how training data are used or synthesized. Practical pipelines combine distillation with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and must address teacher–student capacity mismatch, limited or private data, domain shift, and robustness. Ongoing directions emphasize automated student design, privacy- and data-aware distillation, and task-specific adaptations to make compressed models reliable in production.

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a model compression technique that transfers knowledge from large, complex teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models, enabling practical deployment of state-of-the-art neural networks in resource-constrained environments. This approach addresses critical challenges in deep learning and natural language processing by reducing computational costs, memory requirements, and latency while maintaining competitive performance. Beyond basic compression, knowledge distillation encompasses diverse strategies including soft-target matching, intermediate representation transfer, multi-teacher approaches, and task-aware adaptations that extend its applicability across vision, language processing, speech recognition, and other domains.

papers_seen.author: Ellis
papers_seen.title: On Representation Knowledge Distillation for Graph Neural Networks
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a learning paradigm for boosting resource-efficient graph neural networks (GNNs) using more expressive yet cumbersome teacher models. Past work on distillation for GNNs proposed the Local Structure Preserving loss (LSP), which matches local structural relationships defined over edges across the student and teacher's node embeddings. This paper studies whether preserving the global topology of how the teacher embeds graph data can be a more effective distillation objective for GNNs, as real-world graphs often contain latent interactions and noisy edges. We propose Graph Contrastive Representation Distillation (G-CRD), which uses contrastive learning to implicitly preserve global topology by aligning the student node embeddings to those of the teacher in a shared representation space. Additionally, we introduce an expanded set of benchmarks on large-scale real-world datasets where the performance gap between teacher and student GNNs is non-negligible. Experiments across 4 datasets and 14 heterogeneous GNN architectures show that G-CRD consistently boosts the performance and robustness of lightweight GNNs, outperforming LSP (and a global structure preserving variant of LSP) as well as baselines from 2D computer vision. An analysis of the representational similarity among teacher and student embedding spaces reveals that G-CRD balances preserving local and global relationships, while structure preserving approaches are best at preserving one or the other. Our code is available at https://github.com/chaitjo/efficient-gnns

papers_seen.title: Extract the Knowledge of Graph Neural Networks and Go Beyond it: An Effective Knowledge Distillation Framework
papers_seen.abstract: Semi-supervised learning on graphs is an important problem in the machine learning area. In recent years, state-of-the-art classification methods based on graph neural networks (GNNs) have shown their superiority over traditional ones such as label propagation. However, the sophisticated architectures of these neural models will lead to a complex prediction mechanism, which could not make full use of valuable prior knowledge lying in the data, e.g., structurally correlated nodes tend to have the same class. In this paper, we propose a framework based on knowledge distillation to address the above issues. Our framework extracts the knowledge of an arbitrary learned GNN model (teacher model), and injects it into a well-designed student model. The student model is built with two simple prediction mechanisms, i.e., label propagation and feature transformation, which naturally preserves structure-based and feature-based prior knowledge, respectively. In specific, we design the student model as a trainable combination of parameterized label propagation and feature transformation modules. As a result, the learned student can benefit from both prior knowledge and the knowledge in GNN teachers for more effective predictions. Moreover, the learned student model has a more interpretable prediction process than GNNs. Experimental results show that the learned student model can consistently outperform its corresponding teacher model by 1.4% - 4.7% on average. papers_seen.author: Mcclain
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation in Deep Learning and NLP: Powerful, Practical, but Not a Panacea
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has become a core technique for compressing large models, transferring knowledge across architectures, enabling private or federated workflows, and improving efficiency for deployment in resource-constrained settings. While KD often yields substantial practical gains—reducing model size and inference cost with limited loss in performance—it has important theoretical and empirical limitations related to optimization, data dependence, model and domain heterogeneity, and teacher–student mismatch. A pragmatic stance recognizes KD as a versatile toolset whose effectiveness depends on how it is applied: the choice of distilled targets (logits, features, or relations), the availability or synthesis of data, the use of multiple teachers or staged procedures, and awareness of when distillation can harm or help generalization. This paper argues that KD should be used as part of a broader compression and adaptation strategy guided by empirical diagnostics and appropriate extensions (multi-teacher, zero-shot/data-free, federated/distilled protocols, or self-supervised distillation) rather than as an off-the-shelf cure-all.

papers_seen.author: Martinez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central but Context-Dependent Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile family of techniques that enables high-capacity teacher models to transfer predictive behavior and internal representations to smaller, more efficient student models. KD has matured from soft-label matching into a toolkit that includes representation-level transfer, layer alignment, multi-teacher and teacher-free variants, and integrations with low-precision and architecture-aware compression. KD often yields large efficiency gains with modest performance loss, but its practical success requires attention to teacher quality, student capacity, data selection, and complementary compression methods. A pragmatic approach treats KD as a default component of a compression pipeline while recognizing when additional strategies or task-specific adaptations are necessary.

papers_seen.author: Riley
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Frameworks, Applications, and Practical Considerations
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and versatile technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient student models while transferring valuable learned knowledge. This approach enables the deployment of high-performing deep learning systems in resource-constrained environments across multiple domains including computer vision and natural language processing. Knowledge distillation operates through teacher-student learning frameworks that transfer knowledge beyond simple class labels to encompass soft targets, intermediate representations, and structural behaviors. The technique addresses critical challenges in balancing model capacity with computational efficiency while maintaining competitive performance and enabling practical deployment of state-of-the-art models.

papers_seen.author: Clark
papers_seen.title: A Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related compression techniques transform large, expensive models into smaller, faster, or otherwise more deployable models by transferring knowledge from one model (teacher) to another (student). Research over the past decade has produced a spectrum of methods: representation- and layer-matching, soft-target regularization and teacher-free variants, data-free and adversarial sample synthesis, many-to-many layer alignment for transformer compression, and task-adaptive architecture search with distillation objectives. These approaches address practical constraints—limited compute, privacy of training data, heterogeneous devices, and task-specific requirements—while revealing theoretical connections between KD and regularization. Empirical work shows KD is effective across vision and language tasks, can enable competitive small models for NLP, and remains central to specialized pipelines such as non-autoregressive translation and transformer pruning. Open directions include better matching of inductive biases between teacher and student, principled handling of data absence or privacy, and automated, task-aware compression strategies.

papers_seen.author: Parker
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core Compression Strategy in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a fundamental and versatile technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, deployable models while maintaining competitive performance. By transferring knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to lightweight student networks, KD enables practical deployment of sophisticated deep learning systems in resource-constrained environments. The approach encompasses multiple methodologies including soft-target matching, intermediate representation alignment, and multi-teacher ensemble strategies, with applications spanning computer vision, natural language processing, machine translation, and specialized domains. However, practical success requires careful design choices regarding what knowledge to transfer, teacher-student capacity alignment, data availability, and integration with complementary compression techniques to address deployment-specific challenges.

papers_seen.author: Crawford
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Comprehensive Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a fundamental model compression technique that transfers knowledge from large, high-capacity teacher models to smaller, efficient student models, enabling practical deployment of advanced deep learning and NLP systems in resource-constrained environments. The approach encompasses diverse methodologies including soft-target matching, intermediate representation alignment, and task-aware objectives, often combined with complementary compression techniques such as pruning and quantization. While distillation delivers substantial gains in model size, latency, and memory efficiency, its effectiveness depends critically on careful design choices regarding teacher-student capacity alignment, data availability, and task-specific constraints.

papers_seen.author: Scott
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central and Composable Strategy for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, efficient student models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach transfers knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to resource-constrained students across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, and speech processing. When treated as a core, composable element of integrated compression pipelines and carefully designed with complementary techniques, knowledge distillation enables practical deployment of state-of-the-art models on resource-limited devices while addressing critical challenges in inference latency, memory requirements, and computational efficiency. However, its effectiveness critically depends on careful choices about what knowledge to transfer, teacher-student capacity alignment, data availability strategies, and task-specific adaptations.

papers_seen.author: Wright
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: An Essential Framework for Practical Deep Learning Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models suitable for deployment on resource-constrained devices. This approach transfers knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to smaller student models, enabling substantial reductions in model size, computational cost, and inference latency while maintaining competitive predictive performance. Across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, and speech recognition, knowledge distillation encompasses multiple transfer mechanisms—from soft-target matching to intermediate-representation alignment—and integrates naturally with complementary compression techniques such as pruning and quantization. When carefully designed and applied with attention to teacher-student alignment, data strategies, and task-specific objectives, knowledge distillation becomes an indispensable tool for bringing state-of-the-art deep learning models into practical systems across industries.

papers_seen.author: Shah
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable model-compression paradigm that trains compact student models to reproduce useful behavior of larger teacher models. Across vision and language tasks, KD has evolved from simple softened-logit matching to a flexible toolkit that includes intermediate-feature and attention matching, multi-teacher and online schemes, and data-aware strategies (including synthetic or data-free approaches). When combined with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, and architecture-aware design) and tuned to student capacity and deployment constraints, KD often yields substantial runtime, memory, and energy savings with modest loss in predictive performance. Practical success depends on explicit choices about what to transfer, how to obtain or curate distillation data, how to align objectives and architectures, and how to diagnose failures on low-frequency or safety-critical phenomena. Important open problems include principled teacher–student design, reliable distillation under limited or private data, and preserving robustness, fairness, and specialized behaviors under compression.

papers_seen.author: Valencia
papers_seen.title: Beyond Soft Labels: A Multi-Objective View of Knowledge Distillation for Robust, Efficient Models
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a practical route to compress large neural models for deployment, but treating distillation as merely matching teacher output probabilities limits what can be transferred and how reliably the student will generalize. This paper argues that effective distillation should combine representation-level transfer, channel- and feature-aware objectives, confidence-weighted multi-teacher signals, domain adaptation, and training-time efficiency techniques, while explicitly attending to optimization gaps and fairness concerns. We synthesize evidence across methods and propose a prioritized, pragmatic pipeline for producing compact models that better retain teacher knowledge, scale in production, and reduce unintended harms.

papers_seen.author: Cordova
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Comprehensive Overview
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a fundamental and widely-adopted technique for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable student models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach transfers knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to resource-constrained students through various complementary mechanisms, enabling efficient deployment across diverse domains. KD encompasses multiple methodologies and strategies that address critical practical challenges in real-world deployment scenarios, including computational efficiency, memory constraints, inference latency, and privacy preservation.

papers_seen.author: Hensley
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Essential Techniques for Practical Deep Learning Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression have become fundamental techniques for deploying large neural networks in resource-constrained environments. These methods transfer knowledge from computationally expensive teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models, enabling practical deployment while maintaining competitive performance. The techniques address critical challenges in modern deep learning, including reducing inference latency, memory requirements, and computational costs across diverse domains including computer vision and natural language processing.

papers_seen.author: Chavez
papers_seen.title: Data-Free Knowledge Distillation for Deep Neural Networks
papers_seen.abstract: Recent advances in model compression have provided procedures for compressing large neural networks to a fraction of their original size while retaining most if not all of their accuracy. However, all of these approaches rely on access to the original training set, which might not always be possible if the network to be compressed was trained on a very large dataset, or on a dataset whose release poses privacy or safety concerns as may be the case for biometrics tasks. We present a method for data-free knowledge distillation, which is able to compress deep neural networks trained on large-scale datasets to a fraction of their size leveraging only some extra metadata to be provided with a pretrained model release. We also explore different kinds of metadata that can be used with our method, and discuss tradeoffs involved in using each of them.

papers_seen.author: Green
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a fundamental model compression technique that transfers knowledge from large, high-capacity teacher models to smaller, efficient student models. This approach enables deployment of state-of-the-art deep learning systems in resource-constrained environments while maintaining competitive performance. KD encompasses multiple complementary techniques including soft-label matching, feature-level supervision, intermediate representation alignment, and data-centric strategies. The method addresses critical real-world challenges such as computational efficiency, memory constraints, inference latency, privacy preservation, and device heterogeneity, with applications spanning computer vision, natural language processing, speech recognition, and specialized domains. Success depends on careful selection of transfer targets, appropriate teacher-student pairing, data availability, and matching distillation strategies to specific deployment constraints.
