papers_seen.author: Butler
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and versatile technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, efficient student models while preserving competitive performance. This approach transfers knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to resource-constrained students, enabling practical deployment of state-of-the-art deep learning and NLP systems across diverse domains. Knowledge distillation encompasses multiple complementary mechanisms and methodologies, addressing critical challenges in model efficiency, inference latency, memory consumption, and computational cost. When thoughtfully applied with appropriate design choices and integrated with complementary compression techniques, knowledge distillation provides a practical and flexible framework for achieving reliable, production-ready model compression.

papers_seen.author: Martinez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Foundational, Multi-Strategy Approach for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is most effective when treated not as a single algorithmic trick but as an engineering paradigm that integrates teacher design, student capacity, data strategy, representation objectives, and deployment constraints. When combined with complementary compression (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and deployment-aware practices (privacy, federated protocols, pre-training of small architectures), KD routinely enables compact models that meet latency, memory, and robustness requirements while preserving most of a teacher's performance. However, KD has limits: teacher–student mismatch, data heterogeneity in federated settings, and fairness or distribution-shift failures demand careful, task-aware design and evaluation. The practical position advocated here is that KD should be adopted as a core, configurable component of compression pipelines, with choice of techniques driven by operational constraints and empirical validation.

papers_seen.author: Hopkins
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: What We Know About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-capacity models into smaller, efficient students by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations. A diverse set of mechanisms—soft-target/logit matching, intermediate representation alignment, multi-teacher and online schemes, and data- or privacy-aware variants—have been developed and combined with complementary techniques (e.g., pruning, quantization) to meet deployment constraints. KD is broadly applicable across vision, speech, and natural language tasks, but its practical success depends on teacher–student capacity alignment, data availability, handling of bias and privacy, and task-aware design; outstanding challenges include robustly transferring long-tail knowledge, operating without original training data, and formalizing guarantees for fairness and robustness.

papers_seen.author: Mcclain
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation from Internal Representations
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is typically conducted by training a small model (the student) to mimic a large and cumbersome model (the teacher). The idea is to compress the knowledge from the teacher by using its output probabilities as soft-labels to optimize the student. However, when the teacher is considerably large, there is no guarantee that the internal knowledge of the teacher will be transferred into the student; even if the student closely matches the soft-labels, its internal representations may be considerably different. This internal mismatch can undermine the generalization capabilities originally intended to be transferred from the teacher to the student. In this paper, we propose to distill the internal representations of a large model such as BERT into a simplified version of it. We formulate two ways to distill such representations and various algorithms to conduct the distillation. We experiment with datasets from the GLUE benchmark and consistently show that adding knowledge distillation from internal representations is a more powerful method than only using soft-label distillation.

papers_seen.author: Montoya
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Integration, and Practical Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a foundational technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, efficient student models while preserving competitive performance. This approach transfers knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to resource-constrained students through diverse mechanisms including soft-target matching, intermediate feature alignment, and multi-teacher schemes. When combined with complementary compression methods such as pruning and quantization, and supported by careful task-aware design choices, knowledge distillation enables practical deployment across vision, language, and specialized domains while addressing critical challenges in model size, inference latency, memory consumption, and computational efficiency.

papers_seen.author: Bernard
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, empirically proven approach for compressing large neural networks into efficient models suitable for deployment. Across modalities and tasks — from vision and speech to NLP and retrieval — KD can be implemented through multiple, complementary mechanisms (soft-label supervision, feature mimicry, layer-wise alignment, teacher adaptation, and online co-training) to trade off capacity, compute, and data constraints while retaining much of the teacher performance. Practical KD pipelines benefit from task-aware selection of distilled signals, efficient label generation or online schemes to reduce teacher cost, and teacher/student co-design to close the capacity gap between models.

papers_seen.author: Spencer
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Default, Context‑Aware Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) provides a practical, flexible route to compressing large models into smaller, deployable students by transferring richer supervision than hard labels. Treated as a composable core operation within a broader compression pipeline, KD routinely yields strong size–performance trade‑offs across modalities when paired with complementary techniques and careful, task‑aware design. However, realizing reliable, production‑ready students requires deliberate choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student capacity, how to handle limited or private data, and how to evaluate robustness and rare‑case behaviors.

papers_seen.author: Harrington
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as an Essential but Contextual Tool for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and versatile approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. KD transfers information beyond hard labels and can operate at multiple levels (logits, intermediate features, or contrastive embeddings), enabling large reductions in inference cost and memory while often retaining most of a teacher’s performance. However, KD’s success depends on matching distillation targets, teacher-student capacity, data regimes, and deployment constraints; it is most effective when used as part of an integrated compression strategy rather than as a universal, plug-and-play solution.

papers_seen.author: Cox
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Default for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, engineering-oriented approach to compressing large models into deployable students. By transferring predictive behavior and internal representations through configurable signals, and by composing naturally with pruning, quantization, architecture adaptation, and data-aware strategies, KD routinely produces favorable efficiency–accuracy tradeoffs in language and vision systems. Realizing these gains in production demands task-aware design: choosing appropriate distillation signals, aligning teacher and student capacity, handling limited or private data, and diagnosing robustness, fairness, and distribution-shift risks. When applied as a composable toolkit with explicit monitoring and complementary compression methods, KD provides a practical route to efficient, high-performance models for real-world deployment.

papers_seen.author: Miller
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Improved Accuracy in Spoken Question Answering
papers_seen.abstract: Spoken question answering (SQA) is a challenging task that requires the machine to fully understand the complex spoken documents. Automatic speech recognition (ASR) plays a significant role in the development of QA systems. However, the recent work shows that ASR systems generate highly noisy transcripts, which critically limit the capability of machine comprehension on the SQA task. To address the issue, we present a novel distillation framework. Specifically, we devise a training strategy to perform knowledge distillation (KD) from spoken documents and written counterparts. Our work makes a step towards distilling knowledge from the language model as a supervision signal to lead to better student accuracy by reducing the misalignment between automatic and manual transcriptions. Experiments demonstrate that our approach outperforms several state-of-the-art language models on the Spoken-SQuAD dataset.

papers_seen.author: Cooper
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and versatile technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models suitable for deployment in resource-constrained environments. By transferring knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to compact student networks, knowledge distillation enables substantial reductions in model size, computational cost, memory requirements, and inference latency while maintaining competitive performance. This approach has evolved from simple output-level matching to diverse methodologies encompassing multiple transfer mechanisms, multi-teacher strategies, and data-aware approaches. Knowledge distillation has been successfully applied across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, machine translation, and specialized applications, making it a critical technique for practical deep learning deployment.

papers_seen.author: Peterson
papers_seen.title: The Central Role of Knowledge Distillation in Efficient and Robust NLP Models
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a unifying approach for producing smaller, faster, and often more robust models for NLP and deep learning broadly. When combined with architecture search, layer-wise matching, data-centric techniques, and privacy-aware protocols, distillation enables task-adaptive compression, domain adaptation, and practical deployment under latency, memory, and regulatory constraints. However, the benefits of distillation depend on how knowledge is represented, which data and augmentations are used during transfer, and whether the distillation procedure is aligned with downstream tasks; careful method design—rather than blind teacher-student pairing—is therefore required to realize its full promise.

papers_seen.author: Harper
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as an Essential but Context-Dependent Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has become a fundamental technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, deployable student models while preserving competitive performance. By transferring knowledge from high-capacity teacher models through various mechanisms, knowledge distillation enables practical deployment of deep learning systems in resource-constrained environments across computer vision and natural language processing. However, its effectiveness depends critically on careful design choices, proper alignment of teacher-student capacities, and integration with complementary compression techniques. This position argues that knowledge distillation should be treated as a central, context-aware tool in modern deployment pipelines rather than as a universal solution, with success requiring principled choices about what knowledge to transfer, how to handle data constraints, and how to manage known failure modes.

papers_seen.author: Davidson
papers_seen.title: Robust Re-Identification by Multiple Views Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: To achieve robustness in Re-Identification, standard methods leverage tracking information in a Video-To-Video fashion. However, these solutions face a large drop in performance for single image queries (e.g., Image-To-Video setting). Recent works address this severe degradation by transferring temporal information from a Video-based network to an Image-based one. In this work, we devise a training strategy that allows the transfer of a superior knowledge, arising from a set of views depicting the target object. Our proposal - Views Knowledge Distillation (VKD) - pins this visual variety as a supervision signal within a teacher-student framework, where the teacher educates a student who observes fewer views. As a result, the student outperforms not only its teacher but also the current state-of-the-art in Image-To-Video by a wide margin (6.3% mAP on MARS, 8.6% on Duke-Video-ReId and 5% on VeRi-776). A thorough analysis - on Person, Vehicle and Animal Re-ID - investigates the properties of VKD from a qualitatively and quantitatively perspective. Code is available at https://github.com/aimagelab/VKD.

papers_seen.author: Pham
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Essential Techniques for Efficient Deep Learning and NLP Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression are critical techniques for deploying large neural networks in resource-constrained environments. By transferring knowledge from larger teacher models to smaller student models, these approaches enable significant reductions in model size and computational cost while maintaining competitive accuracy across diverse applications including computer vision, natural language processing, and machine translation. The field has evolved from basic teacher-student knowledge transfer to sophisticated multi-faceted approaches incorporating feature-level matching, data-free methods, and task-aware training protocols.

papers_seen.author: Garcia
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Essential Techniques for Efficient Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and model compression have become indispensable techniques for deploying state-of-the-art deep learning models in resource-constrained environments. By transferring knowledge from large, high-capacity teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models, these methods enable significant reductions in computational requirements, memory usage, and latency while maintaining competitive accuracy. This position argues that knowledge distillation is a versatile and practical family of complementary techniques that, when thoughtfully combined, make sophisticated models deployable across diverse domains including NLP, computer vision, and specialized applications, while addressing critical real-world constraints such as privacy, data heterogeneity, and hardware limitations.

papers_seen.author: Christensen
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Comprehensive Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and practical technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, efficient student models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach transfers knowledge from computationally expensive teacher models to lightweight student networks, enabling deployment in resource-constrained environments. The field encompasses diverse methodologies ranging from soft-target matching to intermediate representation alignment, and is most effective when combined with complementary compression techniques and careful design choices tailored to specific deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Schwartz
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Applications, and Practical Considerations
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a fundamental and versatile technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient student models while preserving competitive performance. By transferring knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to resource-constrained students, KD enables practical deployment across vision, language, and specialized domains. This synthesis examines the core mechanisms of knowledge distillation, its diverse applications, and critical design considerations for achieving effective compression in real-world settings.

papers_seen.author: Ibarra
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Applications, and Practical Considerations
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a versatile and powerful approach for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient student models while maintaining or improving performance. This technique enables the transfer of knowledge from complex teacher models through various mechanisms, addressing critical deployment challenges including computational cost, latency, memory consumption, and resource constraints. Knowledge distillation is increasingly recognized as an essential strategy across computer vision, natural language processing, graph neural networks, and specialized domains, serving not only compression but also regularization, privacy preservation, and knowledge transfer objectives.

papers_seen.author: Johnston
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Comprehensive Framework for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a versatile and empirically effective approach for compressing large neural networks into smaller, deployable student models while preserving competitive performance. Rather than a single technique, knowledge distillation represents a flexible, composable framework that transfers knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to resource-constrained students through multiple complementary mechanisms. When thoughtfully combined with additional compression strategies and adapted to specific task and deployment constraints, knowledge distillation enables practical deployment of state-of-the-art deep learning and NLP systems across diverse domains while addressing critical challenges in computational efficiency, inference latency, memory consumption, and privacy.

papers_seen.author: Clark
papers_seen.title: Collaborative Distillation for Ultra-Resolution Universal Style Transfer
papers_seen.abstract: Universal style transfer methods typically leverage rich representations from deep Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) models (e.g., VGG-19) pre-trained on large collections of images. Despite the effectiveness, its application is heavily constrained by the large model size to handle ultra-resolution images given limited memory. In this work, we present a new knowledge distillation method (named Collaborative Distillation) for encoder-decoder based neural style transfer to reduce the convolutional filters. The main idea is underpinned by a finding that the encoder-decoder pairs construct an exclusive collaborative relationship, which is regarded as a new kind of knowledge for style transfer models. Moreover, to overcome the feature size mismatch when applying collaborative distillation, a linear embedding loss is introduced to drive the student network to learn a linear embedding of the teacher's features. Extensive experiments show the effectiveness of our method when applied to different universal style transfer approaches (WCT and AdaIN), even if the model size is reduced by 15.5 times. Especially, on WCT with the compressed models, we achieve ultra-resolution (over 40 megapixels) universal style transfer on a 12GB GPU for the first time. Further experiments on optimization-based stylization scheme show the generality of our algorithm on different stylization paradigms. Our code and trained models are available at https://github.com/mingsun-tse/collaborative-distillation.

papers_seen.author: Mcdaniel
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: An Indispensable Strategy for Practical Deep Learning Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models suitable for deployment in resource-constrained environments. This approach transfers knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to lightweight student models, enabling practical deployment of state-of-the-art systems while maintaining competitive performance. When strategically applied with careful attention to task-specific requirements and combined with complementary compression techniques, knowledge distillation represents an essential tool for bridging the critical gap between model performance and practical deployment constraints in both deep learning and natural language processing applications.

papers_seen.author: James
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Composable, but Imperfect Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and practically powerful approach to compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. It transfers richer supervision than hard labels—via softened outputs, intermediate feature targets, and relational objectives—and is routinely combined with complementary techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search, data augmentation) to meet real-world deployment constraints. KD often preserves a large fraction of teacher performance while reducing inference cost, but realizing those gains in practice requires attention to teacher–student alignment, the choice of transferred signals, the availability and provenance of distillation data, and evaluations for robustness and bias under domain shift. I argue KD should be treated as a central, composable element of production compression pipelines while recognizing its limits and the engineering needed to close optimization and distributional gaps.

papers_seen.author: Lynn
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large neural models by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from a high-capacity teacher to a smaller student. A broad family of KD methods—including matching teacher output distributions, imitating intermediate features or attention maps, multi-teacher and online schemes, and teacher-free/self-distillation variants—has been developed and frequently combined with pruning, quantization, and architecture search to meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Empirical work shows distilled students can retain much of teacher performance when distillation targets, representation alignment, and data strategies are chosen to suit student capacity and task structure. Key practical issues include selecting appropriate transfer signals, handling limited or private data, and diagnosing failures under distribution shift and long-tail phenomena. Remaining research directions emphasize principled teacher–student alignment, robust distillation under domain shift and data scarcity, and automated, task-aware compression pipelines.

papers_seen.author: Sanders
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Practices in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central method for compressing large neural networks into smaller, deployable models by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from teacher to student. KD encompasses a family of mechanisms—soft-target/logit matching, intermediate-feature and attention imitation, layer-wise alignment, multi-teacher fusion, and data-free or privacy-preserving variants—that are routinely combined with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search) to meet latency, memory, and deployment constraints. Practical success depends on matching distilled signals to student capacity, handling teacher–student architectural mismatches, addressing data availability and privacy, and evaluating robustness and rare-case behavior; these areas remain active challenges for research and engineering.

papers_seen.author: Mack
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Default: A Task-Aware, Composable Approach for Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and empirically effective method for compressing large teacher models into smaller, deployable students. When treated as a core element of a compression pipeline and combined with complementary techniques, KD provides a practical route to reduce latency, memory, and compute while largely preserving task performance. However, its benefits depend on careful teacher–student design, the choice of distilled signals, data strategies, and explicit evaluation of robustness and fairness. I argue KD should be the default starting point for model compression in deep learning and NLP, applied deliberately and adapted to task and deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Decker
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: A Essential Framework for Efficient Deep Learning Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and versatile technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient student models while maintaining competitive performance. By transferring knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to resource-constrained students through multiple mechanisms, distillation enables practical deployment across diverse domains under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Despite its widespread success, effective distillation requires careful attention to teacher-student alignment, data availability, and task-specific design choices.

papers_seen.author: Rodriguez
papers_seen.title: Releasing Graph Neural Networks with Differential Privacy Guarantees
papers_seen.abstract: With the increasing popularity of graph neural networks (GNNs) in several sensitive applications like healthcare and medicine, concerns have been raised over the privacy aspects of trained GNNs. More notably, GNNs are vulnerable to privacy attacks, such as membership inference attacks, even if only black-box access to the trained model is granted. We propose PrivGNN, a privacy-preserving framework for releasing GNN models in a centralized setting. Assuming an access to a public unlabeled graph, PrivGNN provides a framework to release GNN models trained explicitly on public data along with knowledge obtained from the private data in a privacy preserving manner. PrivGNN combines the knowledge-distillation framework with the two noise mechanisms, random subsampling, and noisy labeling, to ensure rigorous privacy guarantees. We theoretically analyze our approach in the Renyi differential privacy framework. Besides, we show the solid experimental performance of our method compared to several baselines adapted for graph-structured data. Our code is available at https://github.com/iyempissy/privGnn.

papers_seen.author: Cohen
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Powerful Tool for Model Compression and Knowledge Transfer in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for training efficient student models by transferring knowledge from larger teacher networks. This paper argues that knowledge distillation is uniquely valuable not only for model compression and deployment on resource-constrained devices, but also for enabling knowledge transfer across diverse model architectures, improving model robustness, and facilitating collaborative learning in distributed and federated settings. The evidence demonstrates that distillation succeeds through multiple mechanisms beyond traditional soft label matching, making it an indispensable method for practical deep learning applications.

papers_seen.author: Bell
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Composable, Central Framework for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is most effective when treated not as a single recipe but as a flexible, composable framework that transfers logits, intermediate representations, or synthesized signals from high-capacity teachers to compact students. In production settings KD routinely yields favorable size–performance trade-offs when combined with complementary techniques (pre-training, pruning, quantization, architecture search, privacy-aware protocols) and when student objectives are adapted to capacity and deployment constraints. However, care is required to avoid transferring undesirable teacher behaviors (bias, overconfidence) and to address optimization gaps on low-frequency phenomena and under limited or private data.

papers_seen.author: Owens
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Multifaceted Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and flexible approach for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students while preserving much of teacher performance. KD methods span logit matching, feature- and layer-level mimicry, ensemble and online schemes, and augmentation-driven strategies. When applied thoughtfully — choosing appropriate distillation targets, considering teacher-student capacity and data availability, and employing methods such as projector layers or data augmentation — KD can deliver compact models that approach teacher accuracy across vision and language tasks. However, realizing these gains requires attention to optimization dynamics and task-specific constraints.

papers_seen.author: Romero
papers_seen.title: What We Know About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a widely adopted approach to compressing large neural networks into smaller, efficient students by transferring information from one or more teacher models. Over the last decade the field has matured from simple soft-target matching to a broad toolkit that includes intermediate-representation matching, attention- and layer-level objectives, multi-teacher and online schemes, data-free distillation, and combinations with pruning, quantization, and architecture search. Empirical evidence shows KD routinely produces substantial reductions in model size and latency while preserving much of the teacher’s performance when design choices—what to transfer, how to construct training data, and how to align teacher and student capacity—are carefully made. Remaining limits include sensitivity to data distribution shifts, propagation of teacher biases or errors, dependence on teacher quality and student capacity, and the need for automated, task-adaptive pipelines that balance efficiency with downstream objectives.

papers_seen.author: Cardenas
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Default, Composable Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible family of techniques for compressing large teacher models into smaller student models by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations. When applied thoughtfully—matching distillation targets to student capacity, addressing data limitations, and integrating complementary compression methods—KD routinely yields strong size–performance tradeoffs that enable deployment in resource-constrained environments. However, KD is not a turnkey solution: its success depends on careful design of teacher signals, student architecture, optimization schedules, and data handling, and practitioners must attend to robustness, privacy, and long-tail behavior when moving distilled models into production.

papers_seen.author: Anderson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile but Context-Sensitive Tool for Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central technique for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students. KD has demonstrated practical value across vision, language, and other domains by reducing inference cost, enabling deployment on resource-constrained devices, and supporting distributed or privacy-sensitive workflows. However, its effectiveness depends strongly on data availability, teacher–student capacity mismatch, domain and task specifics, and system constraints; thus KD should be applied as a composable element of a compression strategy rather than as a universal cure-all.

papers_seen.author: Maldonado
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression have emerged as critical techniques for deploying neural networks in resource-constrained environments. These methods enable the transfer of knowledge from larger teacher models to more compact student models while maintaining predictive performance. Applications span diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and multimodal learning, with approaches ranging from feature-level distillation to collaborative training strategies.

papers_seen.author: Gaines
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression techniques enable the deployment of state-of-the-art deep learning models in resource-constrained environments by transferring knowledge from larger teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models. These approaches have demonstrated significant success across diverse applications including natural language processing, computer vision, and speech processing, achieving substantial reductions in model size and computational cost while maintaining competitive accuracy levels. This synthesis explores the diverse methodologies, theoretical foundations, and practical applications of knowledge distillation and compression techniques in modern deep learning systems.

papers_seen.author: Marks
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: Strengths, Limits, and Deployment Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, empirically validated framework for compressing high-capacity teacher models into smaller, deployable students. By transferring richer supervisory signals than hard labels, KD supports a range of mechanisms (output-level soft targets, intermediate feature matching, multi-teacher and ensemble transfer, and data‐free procedures) that make state-of-the-art models feasible in latency-, memory-, and privacy-constrained settings. When combined with complementary compression techniques and task-aware design, KD routinely yields favorable size–performance tradeoffs across domains from ranking and recommendation to 3D perception and graph-structured prediction. At the same time, KD is context-sensitive: its success depends on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture, the choice of distilled signals, data availability, and careful evaluation for robustness and distribution shift. This paper argues KD should be treated as the default, composable core of practical compression toolkits while highlighting key precautions and concrete implementation recommendations for reliable deployment.

papers_seen.author: Mills
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses high-capacity teacher models into smaller, efficient student models by transferring predictive behavior and internal structure. A mature KD toolkit includes soft-target (logit) matching, intermediate representation and attention alignment, multi-stage or multi-teacher pipelines, and data-aware or data-free synthesis. KD is widely applied across vision, language, speech, graphs, and healthcare to reduce inference latency and memory while often preserving most teacher performance. Practical success depends on matching distilled signals to student capacity, thoughtfully handling data constraints or privacy needs, and combining KD with complementary compression methods to address robustness, fairness, and deployment-specific constraints.

papers_seen.author: Haney
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a family of techniques for transferring information from large teacher models into smaller, deployable student models so students achieve much of the teacher’s performance while meeting resource, latency, or privacy constraints. KD encompasses soft-target (logit) matching, intermediate representation and attention/feature mimicry, multi-teacher and online schemes, and data-aware or data-free variants. Empirical work shows KD is effective across vision, language, graph, and multimodal tasks when teacher–student capacity, distillation signals, and data strategies are chosen to match the target deployment. Practical pipelines commonly combine KD with pruning, quantization, and architecture search; remaining challenges include transferring rare/structural knowledge, robustness under distribution shift, and principled student architecture design.

papers_seen.author: Dunn
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Default, Composable Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, practical framework for compressing large teacher models into smaller, deployable students while retaining much of the original performance. Treated as a composable element of a broader compression pipeline, KD enables substantial reductions in latency, memory, and energy when coupled with task-aware design, careful teacher–student alignment, and complementary techniques. Responsible application requires attention to data availability, capacity mismatch, and the risk of transferring undesirable behaviors, motivating targeted research on robustness, fairness, and data‑free distillation.

papers_seen.author: Alexander
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Context-Sensitive Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and versatile technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, deployable models while preserving much of the teacher's performance. KD has matured into a toolkit that includes soft-target matching, intermediate-feature transfer, multi-teacher schedules, curriculum and data-aware strategies, and domain-specific variants. As a result, KD should be treated as a central element of any production-oriented compression pipeline—but it must be applied with attention to teacher–student capacity alignment, data availability, task requirements, and complementary compression methods to achieve reliable, efficient deployment.

papers_seen.author: Salinas
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Comprehensive Framework
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and versatile technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, efficient student models suitable for deployment in resource-constrained environments. By transferring knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to compact students through various mechanisms, knowledge distillation enables substantial reductions in model size and computational cost while maintaining competitive performance. The field has evolved from simple output-level matching to a comprehensive toolkit encompassing diverse methodologies, complementary techniques, and applications across deep learning and natural language processing domains.

papers_seen.author: Gomez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as an Essential and Practical Framework for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and versatile technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, deployable student models while retaining much of the teacher's performance. This approach transfers knowledge through multiple mechanisms—from soft-target matching to feature alignment and attention transfer—and has been successfully applied across computer vision, natural language processing, speech, and multimodal systems. When thoughtfully combined with complementary compression techniques and adapted to specific task and deployment constraints, knowledge distillation provides reliable solutions for enabling efficient inference in resource-constrained environments. However, realizing its full potential requires careful attention to teacher-student design choices, data strategies, and comprehensive evaluation across robustness and edge-case behaviors.

papers_seen.author: Gray
papers_seen.title: Improved Feature Distillation via Projector Ensemble
papers_seen.abstract: In knowledge distillation, previous feature distillation methods mainly focus on the design of loss functions and the selection of the distilled layers, while the effect of the feature projector between the student and the teacher remains under-explored. In this paper, we first discuss a plausible mechanism of the projector with empirical evidence and then propose a new feature distillation method based on a projector ensemble for further performance improvement. We observe that the student network benefits from a projector even if the feature dimensions of the student and the teacher are the same. Training a student backbone without a projector can be considered as a multi-task learning process, namely achieving discriminative feature extraction for classification and feature matching between the student and the teacher for distillation at the same time. We hypothesize and empirically verify that without a projector, the student network tends to overfit the teacher's feature distributions despite having different architecture and weights initialization. This leads to degradation on the quality of the student's deep features that are eventually used in classification. Adding a projector, on the other hand, disentangles the two learning tasks and helps the student network to focus better on the main feature extraction task while still being able to utilize teacher features as a guidance through the projector. Motivated by the positive effect of the projector in feature distillation, we propose an ensemble of projectors to further improve the quality of student features. Experimental results on different datasets with a series of teacher-student pairs illustrate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

papers_seen.author: Mack
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Default: A Task-Aware, Composable Approach for Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and empirically effective method for compressing large teacher models into smaller, deployable students. When treated as a core element of a compression pipeline and combined with complementary techniques, KD provides a practical route to reduce latency, memory, and compute while largely preserving task performance. However, its benefits depend on careful teacher–student design, the choice of distilled signals, data strategies, and explicit evaluation of robustness and fairness. I argue KD should be the default starting point for model compression in deep learning and NLP, applied deliberately and adapted to task and deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Gibbs
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: What We Know About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-capacity teacher models into smaller student models by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations. Over the past decade KD has grown from simple soft-target matching into a diverse toolkit that includes feature- and layer-level mimicry, multi-teacher and staged procedures, data- and privacy-aware variants, and combinations with pruning, quantization, and architecture search. Empirical work demonstrates that KD can yield substantial efficiency gains while retaining much of teacher performance, but outcomes depend on careful choices about distilled signals, teacher–student alignment, data availability, and complementary compression strategies.

papers_seen.author: Johnson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a fundamental and versatile technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient student models while preserving task performance. This approach transfers knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to resource-constrained students, enabling deployment across diverse domains including natural language processing and computer vision. By operating beyond simple class labels to encompass soft targets, intermediate representations, and structural behaviors, knowledge distillation addresses critical practical constraints including latency, memory efficiency, privacy, and device heterogeneity. Recent advances have extended KD beyond basic teacher-student frameworks to include multi-teacher schemes, feature-level and attention-based objectives, data-free distillation, and combinations with complementary compression techniques, making it indispensable for real-world neural network deployment.

papers_seen.author: Cox
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Deep Learning and NLP: Essential, Composable, and Context-Dependent
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and versatile approach for compressing large teacher models into smaller student models to enable deployment under resource, latency, and privacy constraints. KD techniques—ranging from softened output matching to intermediate-representation and relational transfers—regularly yield large reductions in model size and inference cost while retaining much of teacher performance. However, the value of KD depends on careful alignment of teacher signals with student capacity, appropriate handling of data regimes and domain shift, and integration with complementary compression methods. Treating KD as a central but context-aware component of compression pipelines yields the best trade-offs between efficiency and predictive performance.

papers_seen.author: Lee
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Techniques, Applications, and Practical Considerations
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and versatile technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach transfers knowledge from computationally expensive teacher models to lightweight student networks, enabling deployment on resource-constrained devices across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, graph neural networks, and machine translation. The methodology encompasses multiple mechanisms beyond simple output matching, including intermediate representation alignment, adversarial training, data-free approaches, and integration with complementary compression methods. While offering significant practical benefits for real-world deployment, knowledge distillation requires careful attention to design choices, teacher quality, data strategies, and task-specific objectives to achieve optimal results.

papers_seen.author: Young
papers_seen.title: What Is Known About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible framework for compressing large, high-performing neural models into smaller student models that can be deployed under latency, memory, and compute constraints. KD transfers information beyond hard labels — including soft logits, intermediate representations, and relational or attention signals — and is commonly used in combination with complementary compression methods to meet production budgets. Its effectiveness depends on careful design choices: what to transfer, how to align teacher and student capacity, how to obtain or synthesize data for distillation, and how to evaluate students under realistic distributional and safety constraints. While KD routinely delivers favorable efficiency–accuracy tradeoffs, outstanding challenges remain around robustness, principled teacher–student design, and reliable transfer of rare or structured behaviors.

papers_seen.author: Vasquez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Comprehensive Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and practical technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient student models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach enables the transfer of knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to resource-constrained students through multiple complementary mechanisms, addressing critical challenges in deploying state-of-the-art models on devices with limited computational resources, memory, and energy. The technique has proven effective across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and specialized applications, making it an essential paradigm for practical deep learning deployment.

papers_seen.author: Duarte
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Context-Sensitive Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical framework for transferring knowledge from large teacher models to smaller student models, enabling deployment under tight latency, memory, and privacy constraints. KD encompasses a range of mechanisms—from matching soft logits to aligning intermediate representations and using synthesized or augmented data—and is most effective when integrated with complementary compression techniques and task-aware data strategies. While KD frequently yields strong efficiency–accuracy tradeoffs in vision, language, and speech applications, its benefits depend on careful choices about what to transfer, how to match teacher and student capacity, and how to mitigate optimization and data limitations. Consequently, KD should be treated as a configurable toolkit rather than a one-size-fits-all recipe for model compression.

papers_seen.author: Escobar
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a fundamental technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, efficient student models while preserving competitive performance. By transferring knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to resource-constrained students through multiple mechanisms, distillation enables practical deployment across computer vision, natural language processing, machine translation, and specialized domains. The approach comprises diverse methodologies and is most effective when combined with complementary compression strategies and careful attention to task-specific design choices, though challenges remain in handling data availability, teacher-student alignment, and robustness concerns.

papers_seen.author: Decker
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Practical Effectiveness, Theoretical Trade-offs, and Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a practical and flexible approach to compressing large neural networks while retaining much of their predictive power. Across modalities and tasks—NLP, vision, recommendation, graph learning, and generative modeling—KD-based methods enable faster inference and lower resource use with modest accuracy loss. However, realizing these gains requires attention to teacher quality, the form of supervisory signal (soft vs. hard labels), data augmentation and curriculum, and task-adaptive design. KD can be combined with other compression techniques (pruning, architecture search) and adapted for privacy-preserving or distributed settings. This paper argues that KD is a broadly applicable core strategy for model compression, outlines the mechanisms that make it effective, and provides practical recommendations grounded in empirical and theoretical findings.

papers_seen.author: Potts
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning: Necessity, Methods, and Practical Limitations
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a central technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, deployable models while maintaining competitive performance. By transferring knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to resource-constrained student networks, KD addresses critical challenges in deploying sophisticated deep learning systems across diverse domains. This position argues that while KD is an essential and versatile tool that should be adopted as a foundational component of modern compression pipelines, its effectiveness depends critically on careful task-aware design, proper teacher-student alignment, thoughtful data strategies, and integration with complementary compression methods. KD is not a universal solution but rather a practical framework that must be wielded deliberately to navigate real-world deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Baker
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable strategy for compressing large neural models into smaller, efficient students by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations. KD encompasses multiple complementary mechanisms — soft-label supervision, feature- and attention-level imitation, layer-wise alignment, curriculum and meta-learning of teachers, and data-free or privacy-preserving variants — which together enable deployment of high-performing models under latency, memory, and data constraints. Practical success depends on matching distilled signals to student capacity, handling teacher–student architectural mismatches, and addressing robustness and data-availability challenges. This synthesis summarizes prevailing methods, empirical patterns, and practical considerations for KD in vision and NLP settings.

papers_seen.author: Higgins
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a model compression technique that enables the efficient deployment of large neural networks by training smaller student models to mimic the behavior of larger teacher models. This approach has become fundamental across computer vision, natural language processing, and specialized domains, addressing the critical challenge of reducing computational overhead and memory requirements while maintaining competitive performance. The technique encompasses diverse strategies ranging from soft label guidance to intermediate layer alignment and operates through the transfer of learned knowledge from teacher to student networks.

papers_seen.author: Baker
papers_seen.title: Rejuvenating Low-Frequency Words: Making the Most of Parallel Data in Non-Autoregressive Translation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is commonly used to construct synthetic data for training non-autoregressive translation (NAT) models. However, there exists a discrepancy on low-frequency words between the distilled and the original data, leading to more errors on predicting low-frequency words. To alleviate the problem, we directly expose the raw data into NAT by leveraging pretraining. By analyzing directed alignments, we found that KD makes low-frequency source words aligned with targets more deterministically but fails to align sufficient low-frequency words from target to source. Accordingly, we propose reverse KD to rejuvenate more alignments for low-frequency target words. To make the most of authentic and synthetic data, we combine these complementary approaches as a new training strategy for further boosting NAT performance. We conduct experiments on five translation benchmarks over two advanced architectures. Results demonstrate that the proposed approach can significantly and universally improve translation quality by reducing translation errors on low-frequency words. Encouragingly, our approach achieves 28.2 and 33.9 BLEU points on the WMT14 English-German and WMT16 Romanian-English datasets, respectively. Our code, data, and trained models are available at \url{https://github.com/alphadl/RLFW-NAT}.

papers_seen.author: Snyder
papers_seen.title: Treating Knowledge Distillation as the Core, Composable Framework for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is more than a single algorithmic trick: it is a flexible, deployable framework that, when combined with complementary compression methods and data strategies, produces compact models that retain much of teacher performance. Practical KD emphasizes what signals to transfer (logits, features, attention, or relational structure), how to handle limited or private data, and how to align teacher and student capacity; best results arise when distillation is integrated into pipelines that include architecture-aware design, pruning/quantization, and data synthesis or augmentation. This synthesis argues that KD should be treated as a composable core of compression toolkits for real-world deep learning and NLP deployment, and offers concrete methodological recommendations for practitioners.

papers_seen.author: Harris
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: A Practical Strategy for Deploying Deep Learning and NLP Models
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a powerful and practical technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. By transferring knowledge from computationally expensive teacher models to lightweight student networks, KD enables the deployment of state-of-the-art models on resource-constrained devices. While KD is not a universal solution and requires careful design choices, when combined with complementary strategies such as representation-level transfer, data-aware techniques, and task-specific optimization, it can preserve much of the teacher's performance while substantially reducing inference costs and memory requirements. This makes KD an essential strategy for practical deep learning deployment across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, and specialized applications.

papers_seen.author: Morris
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large, high-capacity teacher models into smaller, efficient student models by transferring information beyond hard labels. Research expands the basic soft-target paradigm into methods that align intermediate representations, use multi-teacher or online protocols, and operate under constrained data regimes (including data-free and adversarial sample generation). Distillation is widely applied in NLP (including compressed pretrained language models and domain-adaptive students), vision, multimodal systems, and large-scale industrial training pipelines. Practical success depends on matching distillation signals to student capacity, handling data availability and domain shift, and combining distillation with complementary compression techniques while accounting for robustness and privacy concerns.

papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Context-Sensitive Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and versatile technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, deployable models while preserving much of the teacher's performance. KD has matured into a toolkit that includes soft-target matching, intermediate-feature transfer, multi-teacher schedules, curriculum and data-aware strategies, and domain-specific variants. As a result, KD should be treated as a central element of any production-oriented compression pipeline—but it must be applied with attention to teacher–student capacity alignment, data availability, task requirements, and complementary compression methods to achieve reliable, efficient deployment.

papers_seen.author: Carrillo
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Practice, and Open Challenges
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a core approach for compressing large deep learning models into smaller, deployable students by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from teacher models. KD has matured into a flexible family of techniques—logit or soft-target matching, intermediate feature and attention transfer, multi-teacher strategies, self-distillation, and data- or privacy-aware variants—that can be combined with pruning, quantization, and architecture search to meet latency, memory, and deployment constraints. Empirical work shows KD often preserves much of teacher performance across vision, language, speech, and other modalities, but practical success depends on student capacity, teacher–student alignment, data availability, and careful engineering of objectives and schedules.

papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be treated as the default, central technique in model-compression pipelines for deep learning and NLP. KD routinely delivers strong size–performance trade-offs by transferring predictive behavior and intermediate structure from large teachers to compact students, and it composes naturally with pruning, quantization, and architecture search to meet real deployment constraints. Realizing KD’s benefits in production requires context-sensitive design: align teacher and student capacity, choose distillation targets suited to the task, handle limited or private data with specialized methods, and evaluate robustness and distributional generalization. When applied thoughtfully, KD enables practical, deployable models that balance accuracy, latency, memory, and privacy constraints.

papers_seen.author: Newton
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: A Central Yet Context-Dependent Strategy for Practical Deep Learning Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression have emerged as fundamental techniques for deploying large neural networks in resource-constrained environments. By transferring knowledge from computationally expensive teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models, these methods achieve significant reductions in model size, inference latency, and memory requirements while maintaining competitive performance. However, the effectiveness of knowledge distillation depends critically on careful alignment of distillation targets, teacher-student capacity, data availability, and deployment constraints. This paper argues that knowledge distillation is a versatile and essential toolkit for practical deployment, but its success requires principled design choices rather than application as a universal solution.

The field encompasses multiple methodologies ranging from soft-target matching and feature-level imitation to multi-teacher pipelines and data-free approaches, addressing critical practical challenges in model deployment while presenting important limitations that require careful consideration.

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression transfer predictive behavior or internal structure from large teacher models to smaller student models so that compact models can run under latency, memory, and privacy constraints while retaining much of the original performance. A spectrum of techniques—matching teacher output distributions, aligning intermediate representations, attention- or correlation-based feature imitation, task-adaptive architecture search, and data-side methods such as augmentation or synthetic example generation—have been developed and combined in practice. Success depends on choices about what signal to transfer, how to align teacher and student architectures, and how to prepare or augment the data used for distillation; open problems include robust transfer under distribution shift, privacy-preserving and data-free distillation, and principled teacher design for specific student architectures and deployment constraints.

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large, high-capacity teacher models into smaller, efficient student models by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations. Practical deployment typically combines distillation with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and requires careful choices about distilled targets, teacher–student capacity alignment, data handling (including data-free scenarios), and robustness to distribution shift. Despite wide empirical success across vision, speech, and NLP, open problems remain in principled multi-teacher fusion, data- and privacy-aware distillation, and theory-grounded prescriptions for design choices.

papers_seen.author: James
papers_seen.title: Robust Cross-Modal Representation Learning with Progressive Self-Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: The learning objective of vision-language approach of CLIP does not effectively account for the noisy many-to-many correspondences found in web-harvested image captioning datasets, which contributes to its compute and data inefficiency. To address this challenge, we introduce a novel training framework based on cross-modal contrastive learning that uses progressive self-distillation and soft image-text alignments to more efficiently learn robust representations from noisy data. Our model distills its own knowledge to dynamically generate soft-alignment targets for a subset of images and captions in every minibatch, which are then used to update its parameters. Extensive evaluation across 14 benchmark datasets shows that our method consistently outperforms its CLIP counterpart in multiple settings, including: (a) zero-shot classification, (b) linear probe transfer, and (c) image-text retrieval, without incurring added computational cost. Analysis using an ImageNet-based robustness test-bed reveals that our method offers better effective robustness to natural distribution shifts compared to both ImageNet-trained models and CLIP itself. Lastly, pretraining with datasets spanning two orders of magnitude in size shows that our improvements over CLIP tend to scale with number of training examples.

papers_seen.author: Herrera
papers_seen.title: Compressing GANs using Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) have been used in several machine learning tasks such as domain transfer, super resolution, and synthetic data generation. State-of-the-art GANs often use tens of millions of parameters, making them expensive to deploy for applications in low SWAP (size, weight, and power) hardware, such as mobile devices, and for applications with real time capabilities. There has been no work found to reduce the number of parameters used in GANs. Therefore, we propose a method to compress GANs using knowledge distillation techniques, in which a smaller "student" GAN learns to mimic a larger "teacher" GAN. We show that the distillation methods used on MNIST, CIFAR-10, and Celeb-A datasets can compress teacher GANs at ratios of 1669:1, 58:1, and 87:1, respectively, while retaining the quality of the generated image. From our experiments, we observe a qualitative limit for GAN's compression. Moreover, we observe that, with a fixed parameter budget, compressed GANs outperform GANs trained using standard training methods. We conjecture that this is partially owing to the optimization landscape of over-parameterized GANs which allows efficient training using alternating gradient descent. Thus, training an over-parameterized GAN followed by our proposed compression scheme provides a high quality generative model with a small number of parameters.

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model compression techniques transform large, costly models into smaller, faster, or more private models while retaining much of the original performance. Important open problems remain in data heterogeneity, robustness transfer, and principled teacher-student design for diverse deployment constraints.
